Several virtual and in-person activities will be run including workshops to explore what the pregnancy journey looks like for women in each country and provide the opportunity to share expertise and create the IUPJ network. The IUPJ network aims to develop a strong nurturing relationship for those new to research and to ensure the sharing of research skills across the two countries. We hope this network grant will lead to a well-formed network and future research programme across the two countries that brings psychology and midwifery together.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Understanding the relationship between neighbourhood environments and children's health and well-being: A Bangladesh-UK knowledge sharing network for
descriptions:
High population growth in major cities is leading to high-density living in many urban areas in the Global South, with apartment buildings encroaching on open spaces, parks, playgrounds, and public amenities. While studies have shown the adverse effects of the built environment on the physical and mental health of adults, little is known about its impact on children. We aim to explore the connections between the built environment and children's mental health in the Global South, with a primary focus on Bangladesh, where 60% of the urban population are children. By exploring children’s own perceptions using their drawings as stimuli for focus group discussions, we aim to examine what features of the environment contribute to their sense of well-being. The potential impact of this research is significant and could lead to the co-creation of more child-friendly urban environments, contributing to multiple sustainable development goals.  
The UK has made much progress toward creating child-friendly urban environments. Best practice, however, cannot be transplanted from the global North to the global South, and culture and context must be central to any knowledge-sharing endeavour. We aim to develop a networking initiative to facilitate collaboration between researchers from Bangladesh, India and the UK. We will leverage effective practices that harvest the knowledge needed to foster the development of child-friendly cities. Our activity will facilitate the crafting of a research proposal that will inform the development of sustainable and scalable practices that will inform policy and practice in the Global South.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: STI-Net: Reducing transmission of sexually transmitted infections (STI) and STI antimicrobial resistance in Brazil: Harnessing molecular testing techn
descriptions:
Sexually transmitted infections (STIs) can have severe consequences for human health and are a major public health concern worldwide. Outbreaks of STIs can spread rapidly, as recently highlighted by the global mpox epidemic, and growing antibiotic resistance in bacterial STIs like gonorrhoea is restricting treatment options. In Brazil, very little is known about the frequency of STIs, antibiotic resistance in STIs and who is most affected. People are usually treated for STI symptoms without getting specific tests. This means they may get antibiotics that do not work and can pass on a resistant STI to their partners, leading to outbreaks and community spread. 
The lack of data on STIs and antibiotic resistance in STIs in Brazil has made it difficult to develop healthcare services and public health interventions for those in greatest need. Through our network we aim to hold workshops to develop a research programme that uses state-of-the-art testing and communications technology to generate data on STI frequency and evidence to design STI healthcare services and inform public health responses in Brazil. We aim to build innovative digital reporting systems for STI test results so that healthcare providers can treat infections with effective antibiotics in real time and public health departments can respond rapidly to STI outbreaks and STI antibiotic resistance. We believe our partnership could help deliver a step change in the control of STIs and antibiotic resistance in Brazil and will provide a benchmark for high-quality healthcare and public health preparedness for STIs in similar countries.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Hybrid Fiber-Wireless 2-Dimensional Flexible Cross Correlation (2-D FCC) OCDMA For Future 6G Network Massive Accessibility
descriptions:
Ubiquitous accessibility to communication networks has become essential to the digital transformation of industrial and business processes and customer experiences. The Sixth-Generation (6G) networks are expected to offer communication capacity, reliability and massive connectivity superior to those achievable by 5G networks. 6G networks harness various multiple access techniques, including Wavelength Division Multiple Access (WDMA),Time Division Multiple Access (TDMA), and Optical Code Division Multiple Access (OCDMA), to support massive, high-data-rate accessibility envisioned for many 6G application scenarios, e.g., industrial Internet of things (IIoT). However, WDMA and TDMA have limitations in the number of users that they can accommodate without degrading data rate per user. In OCDMA, the emerging  2-dimensional (wavelength and time) coding approaches present new opportunities to mitigate the impairments, such as multiple-access interference (MAI), suffered by existing one-dimensional (wavelength) optical coding. 
In this networking project, we will develop novel Hybrid Fiber-Wireless 2-Dimensional Flexible Cross Correlation (2-D FCC) OCDMA for 6G network massive accessibility. The 2-D FCC OCDMA will improve data transmission rates through optimizing bandwidth utilization, eliminating MAI, and improving the bit error rate (BER). This research work will be embarked in three phases. The first phase is to formulate the 2-D FCC algorithm. The second phase is to devise and analyze the Hybrid Fiber-Wireless 2-D FCC algorithm with Optisystem simulation tools. The final phase is to develop and validate a prototype of Hybrid Fiber-Wireless 2-D FCC OCDMA for supporting 6G network massive accessibility in typical use cases such as IIoT.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Promoting innovation ecosystems in the informal sector, decent work and inclusive economic growth in LDCs
descriptions:
We seek funding for an interdisciplinary research on the factors that shape innovation ecosystem (knowledge and technology transfers) within the informal economy of two developing countries, Kenya and Uganda, in order to promote decent work and economic growth. We focus on the two countries because they need urgent help, and they are prioritised in the International Science Partnerships Fund (the "ISPF") call: Kenya, a prioritised-Official Development Assistant (ODA) country and Uganda, a Least Developed Country (LDC) on the development assistance committee (DAC) list. Also, our proposal meets the second ISPF call requirement by targeting the Sustainable Development Goal 8 (SDG8): decent work and economic growth.
Kenya and Uganda will massively benefit from this project. By investigating the factors that shape innovation ecosystem within the informal economy, stakeholders in the Kenyan and Ugandan informal economy will have access to relevant knowledge that will change policy and practice, and transition the sector into a high-productive, high-growth and a decent-job sector. Currently, like in most developing countries (DCs), over 9 out of 10 jobs created in Kenya and Uganda are in the informal economy but these jobs are carried out under precarious conditions (IMF, 2017; World Bank, 2020; Igudia, 2020). Also, innovation in the informal economy will reduce inequality (SDG10) by generating decent-employment opportunities for disadvantaged groups especially youths and women in Kenya and Uganda. Finally, the proposed research will have wider impacts and applications to DCs, especially sub-Saharan African countries because they share similar characteristics, particularly, large informal economy.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Smart Digital Platform Supporting Indigenous Communities threatened by Natural Disasters and Environmental Degradation
descriptions:
Today, hardly a week passes by without disasters disrupting people’s lives around the world. Some of the most vulnerable and exposed regions can be found across Africa and Asia, where natural hazards, such as flooding, tropical cyclones, landslides, and droughts, affect the life of millions of indigenous people. The severity and frequency of these events are exacerbated by climate change, drastically affecting the indigenous communities. Simultaneously, the environmental degradation of terrestrial and aquatic environments threatens the health and well-being of communities, amid the historic legacy of poorly regulated industrial development and the current pressures of internal migration to urban areas. Although significant advances have been achieved in increasing community resilience to disasters and improving environmental monitoring to reduce environmental degradation, the success of these efforts are often limited by restrictions of available ICT infrastructure and the lack of the ability to collect and integrate relevant monitoring data.  
The project will bring together experts from Duy Tan University (Vietnam), York University and Queen’s University Belfast (UK), and academic partners from Africa including Tanzania and Ghana, to address the pressing problems in relation to disaster resilience and environmental degradation faced by indigenous communities. We will develop a network that fosters smart digital technologies utilising the contemporary wireless infrastructure (e.g., Internet-of-Things (IoT), cellular networks, aerial networks) together with artificial intelligence (AI), real-time optimisation, big data analytics, to tackle the lack of available ICT infrastructure to support the life of indigenous people.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: UK-ASEAN Network on AI-Enabled Healthcare Research and Innovation using Wearable Technologies (AIWT4Care)
descriptions:
AIWT4Care is a new initiative dedicated to transform healthcare in the ASEAN region, by integrating wearable technologies and AI. This initiative is all about ensuring people in ASEAN countries like Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Thailand, and Vietnam achieve better health and wellbeing, a vision that resonates with the United Nations' Sustainable Development Goals.
 
What makes AIWT4Care stand out is its potential to shift healthcare from being reactive to proactive. Through continuous health monitoring and AI's real-time data analysis, we can anticipate and address health issues earlier. This not only promises better individual healthcare but also a more robust and preventive community health strategy.
AIWT4Care seeks to establish a collaborative research network between the UK and ASEAN to address EPSRC-identified challenges related to population health and prevention through healthier environments. By pooling our resources and expertise, we can lead the way in digital health innovations, paving the path toward Universal Health Coverage and more equitable health outcomes across societies.
AIWT4Care is exciting because it brings together a diverse group of researchers to spark innovation and share knowledge in ways that could redefine global health practices. It will facilitate networking, collaboration, and the development of new research concepts that cross traditional disciplinary boundaries.
This initiative will also prepare the ground for future research and funding opportunities, fostering a new generation of talent in the healthcare innovation sector. AIWT4Care embodies the spirit of international cooperation and shared knowledge, with the ultimate aim of enhancing healthcare for people everywhere.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Preparing for Pre-Hospital Emergency Care in Vietnam
descriptions:
The WHO identifies that trauma is the leading cause of death in young people globally. This ground-breaking project has been specifically designed to respond to an urgent need to develop and implement pre-hospital emergency care (PHEC) services in Vietnam. The Vietnamese government has recognised that the current system to be rapidly scaled up to protect the public.
This is a first stage in the development of context specific, effective, and efficient pre-hospital care model which will ultimately impact on the whole country. It will include the first steps into patient centred research, the pinnacle of effective emergency and trauma evidence-based practice. Systematic review into current PHEC in emerging economy countries and prepare the way for robust research using a retrospective review of emergency and trauma patient records, this will include the current emergency service (115) and hospitals in Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City.  
Over the past two decades Vietnam’s health services have expanded beyond recognition, with the exception of PHEC. 115 in Hanoi has 15 ambulances for 10 million population, and few specialists. As from 01.01.24 the law is changing to allow paramedics/emergency technicians training. The National University’s Faculty of Emergency and Trauma are keen to take on the challenge and start the development of this new professional group. Having studied other countries, the UK has a system that is judged appropriate for adaption to develop a Vietnamese context specific service. Birmingham City University an NHS paramedic education provider will work with the National University and partners. 
248 words

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Optimising neglected zoonotic disease (NZD) surveillance and control in Sub-Saharan Africa through changing hearts, minds and techniques.
descriptions:
Neglected Tropical Diseases (NTDs) are a group of diseases that affect over a billion people in developing countries, causing hundreds of thousands of deaths annually and billions of dollars in remedial costs or lost productivity. The United Nations seeks to eradicate NTDs by 2030 (Sustainable Development Goal 3; Target 3.3) but they report this is unlikely, despite a programme of disease-reduction activities. The World Health Organisation has called for urgent in-country research, new approaches and simplified strategies to control NTDS. 
We are a multidisciplinary group with extensive experience in the evaluation and control of zoonotic diseases, covering both human and animal aspects, and in human behaviour. We seek to reduce the impact of neglected zoonotic diseases, a subset of NTDs, by evaluating the current status of four exemplar diseases in three countries, relevant actors’ attitudes and behaviours, and their understanding of challenges to eradication. We will then explore how eradication of these diseases might be optimised through targeted interventions, better government agency collaboration, transdisciplinary health messaging, and collaborative medical and veterinary tertiary education. 
This comprehensive, One Health approach will be largely exploratory for this grant, but will provide important insights into all aspects of zoonotic disease control, from those affected by such diseases, to those responsible for their eradication, from students to professionals.  It will result in new understanding and better strategies that will be developed further in a subsequent grant application, but even without that, will assist policymakers and implementation personnel as they strive to reach the SDG3 target.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Advancing Microscopy and Image Analysis: OpenFlexure Workshops for Research Innovation
descriptions:
Access to advanced microscopy equipment is pivotal in fields like medical diagnostics, biological research, and materials science. Yet, many Kenyan institutions lack the resources for state-of-the-art microscopes, leading to adverse consequences.
To address these pressing challenges, our collaborative initiative between Meru University of Science and Technology (MUST) and the University of Cambridge aims to enhance local research and industry capabilities in developing affordable, high-performance open-source microscopes. Leveraging the expertise of the University of Cambridge, with a particular emphasis on their recent OpenFlexure Microscope (OFM), we have designed a comprehensive program of engaging activities.
This program includes hands-on workshops held in Kenya, allowing participants to learn the construction of OFMs and gain expertise in OFM software and microscope automation. These workshops will also cover microscopy image analysis, incorporating the application of machine learning models. To facilitate ongoing knowledge exchange, we plan to conduct monthly webinars and establish discussion forums connecting scientists from both institutions.
Our collaboration will extend to collaborative research efforts and joint publications, further enhancing research output. We will actively explore available open grants to sustain this collaboration, ensuring its long-term success.
The overarching future goal of our initiative is to elevate the field of microscopy in Kenya by fostering local research talent and transferring technology expertise. As part of this effort, we aspire to establish a microscopy imaging facility at MUST, which will not only support research and development but also drive innovation in microscopy across the country.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Ending Cryptococcal meningitis deaths by 2030: A network for change in Vietnam
descriptions:
This network brings together an interdisciplinary team of experts in the field of medical mycology and HIV-associated fungal infection from Vietnam, South Africa and UK to improve outcomes for patients with cryptococcal meningitis (CM) in Vietnam. 
CM is a life-threatening disease responsible for over 110,000 deaths each year and accounting for 19% of all HIV-associated mortality globally. Two landmark African-based trials, conducted by members of this network, have led to updated WHO guidelines for the safe and effective treatment of CM using single high-dose liposomal amphotericin B (lAmB) (AMBITION regimen). This regimen has been adopted into national guidelines in a number of African countries (with support from network members) but is yet to be introduced in Vietnam.  
Significant strategic changes in practice (moving from standard dose lAmB (3mg/kg/day for 7 days) to single high-dose (10mg/kg, day 1) and lack of experience in administering lAmB (where access has been limited) could be met with hesitation from practitioners and is a potential barrier to effective implementation of this life-saving treatment.  
The aim of this project is to support integration of the AMBITION regimen into Vietnamese national guidelines and aid effective implementation of the regimen into routine care settings. Successful roll-out of these new guidelines could significantly reduce CM mortality in Vietnam and contribute towards reducing HIV-related deaths; a major aim of the 2030 Sustainable Development Goals.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Establishing an international clinical trials network for dengue virus infection
descriptions:
Dengue is the most abundant mosquito-borne virus globally, causing around 100 million symptomatic infections yearly. Unfortunately, there are no treatments which affect the course of dengue; there are no anti-viral medications to prevent people developing severe disease, and no specific treatments for those with severe dengue. However, research efforts have highlighted several potential therapeutic approaches which should be tested in clinical trials. The first goal of this meeting is to prioritise potential treatments for our proposed clinical trials in dengue.  
Our second goal is to harmonise approaches to measuring outcomes in dengue trials; we have already begun a formal process to develop a consensus Core Outcome Set for dengue clinical trials by performing an extensive literature review and engaging key stakeholders including experts in clinical trials, dengue management and patients with lived experience. At the meeting we will gather expert working groups for the final round of the delphi process and finalise an agreed Core Outcome Set for dengue clinical trials. 
As dengue affects different populations in different countries, a diverse portfolio of research centers recruiting to clinical trials is essential to ensure that results are broadly applicable. Our third goal is to formally establish a network of researchers in dengue endemic regions to design and lead clinical trials for dengue; biostatisticians, experts in clinical trial methodology and clinical researchers from 10 countries will form the network, and we anticipate that researchers from institutions in endemic regions will become co-applicants on a trial proposal to be submitted next year. This work will be of special significance to several DAC-listed countries, to include Brazil, Thailand, Malaysia, and Viet Nam.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Integrating digital transformation and circular economy for decarbonised construction & demolition waste diversion: enhancing Vietnam and UK’s researc
descriptions: In 2021, the construction industry (CI) accounted for a substantial 34% of total energy consumption and approximately 37% of energy and CO2 emissions [1]. It also generated a significant volume of construction and demolition waste (C&DW), a major component of municipal solid waste in Vietnam and other ODA countries. Addressing C&DW management is vital for the 2050 zero-carbon target. Digitalization can aid decarbonization [2], yet a notable gap exists in its adoption within the CI, especially in C&DW management. Enter AIRINESS: Our initiative connects scholars and practitioners from the UK, Vietnam, and ODA countries to explore Circular Economy (CE) applications for C&DW decarbonization via digital transformation. We focus on leveraging emerging digital technologies to tackle global C&DW challenges, establish measurable carbon emission indicators for CE-oriented C&DW management, and promote the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) for efficient C&DW sorting and reuse. AIRINESS fosters research collaboration between Vietnam (Hanoi University of Civil Engineering - HUCE, Hochiminh City University of Technology - HCMUT) and the UK (Brunel University London -Brunel) in optimizing energy recovery from C&DW and utilizing integrated digital technologies for C&DW monitoring and waste management planning. Early career researchers from the UK and ODA countries will benefit from exchanges and guest lectures through the networking activities. Furthermore, AIRINESS shares its latest research outcomes with non-academic stakeholders like policymakers and NGOs to support Net-Zero objectives. Our results extend to Laos (National University of Laos - NUoL) and Cambodia (Institute of Technology of Cambodia - ITC), enhancing our impact and network expansion.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: UK-VN Scientific Network for Hydrogen and Related Technologies for Net Zero
descriptions:
The UK and Vietnam have shown significant commitments to address grand challenges related to the global climate change and moving towards sustainable future with net zero pollution. The UK together with the European Union and other nations recently demonstrate strong support of $15.5 billion via a Just Energy Transition Partnership package for Vietnam's ambitious Net Zero 2050 goal. Hydrogen and related technologies (such as renewable energies like wind and solar) are identified to be key players in the transition to the Net Zero.
This proposal aims to establish a UK-Vietnam scientific network for Net Zero to promote scientific exchange and research activities contributing to the two nations' commitments to the Net Zero goal. The network will focus on hydrogen, the roles of renewable energies in hydrogen, and hydrogen storage and distribution for future hydrogen economy. The network will connect researchers, engineers and students in relevant disciplines such as chemistry, materials, structures, mechanical engineering and policy in the two countries to exchange the knowledge and facilitate collaborations towards addressing grand challenges related to the Net Zero in Vietnam and UK. The network will be led by the two nation's best universities in science and technology - Imperial College London (ICL, UK) and Hanoi University of Science and Technology (HUST, Vietnam). In addition, a pilot study between ICL and HUST will be carried out to study the feasibility of using an existing metals in gas pipeline (or liquified gas vessels) for hydrogen storage and distribution in future.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: UK-South Africa partnership on Biovigilance utilising next-generation sequencing technology across the One Heath continuum
descriptions:
The COVID-19 pandemic highlighted the importance of frontier science and next-generation sequencing (NGS), especially in understanding and responding to the impacts of emerging infectious diseases on human health. Genomic methods are rapidly becoming key tools for continuous surveillance of antimicrobial resistance (AMR), especially across the One Health continuum which integrates humans, animals, and environmental settings. AMR is a global crisis threatening the lifesaving role of antibiotics upon which modern medicine is built. 
Revolutionising methodologies are increasingly utilised across high-income countries, but low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) lag behind often due to insufficient funding and lack of appropriate specialist training. At the same time, they suffer from a high burden of foodborne disease due to poor food hygiene and abundant resistant bacteria.  South Africa is limited in expertise in research funding and technology to quantitively assess the AMR important pathogens across the One Health continuum and largely relies on decades-old methods to undertake microbiological safety testing. This warrants the need to establish a network with experts with knowledge and expertise to address the problem of food safety along the food chain. 
We will create an international network on advanced, proactive farm to food biovigilance linking researchers at the University of Cape Town with researchers in the UK and other LMICs who have worked extensively on AMR transmission across the One Health continuum. This will connect the South African researchers with One Health communities across the world to increase capacity for innovative and effective biovigilance tools and solutions using NGS. This work will benefit communities in South Africa, but also Bangladesh, Kenya and Egypt .

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: School uniforms and ideologies of harm: transnational policies, perspectives, and action
descriptions:
Stemming from its British colonial roots, school uniform represents a particular culture of schooling in many parts of the world. Assumptions linking uniform to increased discipline and improved educational outcomes abound, despite a near-complete absence of evidence. School uniform research has thus far concentrated on critical analyses of policies, rules, and guidance published on school websites, arguing that dress codes are frequently underwritten with explicit and implicit gender, class, and racial biases, and therefore that they represent significant potential for harm. However, this has yet to be examined experimentally, or from the perspectives of uniform wearers themselves. Drawing together an interdisciplinary team of researchers, activists, and policymakers, the proposed Wearable Ideologies School Uniform Network will develop a major international project about gender ideologies and school uniform. Combining social semiotics, gender studies, and behavioral psychology, we propose a series of innovative experiments to interrogate what school uniforms ‘say’ about gender, and how children, adults, teachers, and policy makers perform, interpret, and project diverse identities through uniforms and uniform-wearing. 
Focusing comparatively on schools in the UK, South Africa, and Thailand, the Network seeks funding to pump-prime research and public and policy engagement activities, which will provide proof-of-concept and lead directly to a large grant bid for a scaled-up project (2025). Complementing psychological experiments and surveying with engagement and impact activities, we position pupils, teachers, and educational bodies not only as objects of analysis, but as partners in the design of the future research agenda and its impacts on public discourse and policymaking.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Strengthening Global Partnerships: Digital Twinning for Stroke Care in Vietnam and Indonesia
descriptions: Recent advances of digital technologies have potential to change the landscape of health care sector. The project's goal is to establish international partnerships bridging researchers, doctors, policy makers, and practitioners from Vietnam, Indonesia, India, and the UK to harness 'digital twinning' technology for improved stroke care. Digital twinning, while widely investigated in various fields, is a novel approach in stroke care. By creating virtual replicas of patients' brains and stroke histories, doctors can enhance decision-making and treatment prediction. This initiative forms a global network of healthcare experts/researchers collaborating to investigate the potential and challenges of digital twins for stroke patients. This interdisciplinary collaboration enables the exchange of knowledge and experiences, fostering a united global community dedicated to advancing stroke care. Stroke poses a significant global health concern, with particular urgency in countries like Vietnam and Indonesia where minor-stroke patients often receive inadequate care, leading to severe consequences. Through these partnerships, the project aims to explore and develop more effective stroke prevention and treatment methods, resulting in better patient outcomes, faster interventions, and lives saved. This collaboration with UK experts promises to make a tangible impact on stroke patients' lives and strengthen the global healthcare community in Vietnam/Indonesia, aligning with UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) related to health, innovation, and partnerships (SDG 3 'Good health and well-being,' SDG 9 'Industry, innovation and infrastructure,' and SDG 17 'Partnerships for the goals'). The project anticipates exciting discoveries and opportunities as it works towards enhancing global partnerships in digital twinning for stroke care.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Brazil-UK Network on Healthy Aging and Inequalities
descriptions:
Our grant proposal aims to establish a robust network between Brazil and the UK, with a central focus on healthy ageing and inequalities. This research area was chosen because it addresses a significant and pressing concern shared by both nations: the need to ensure that as people live longer, they do so in good health and with a high quality of life, especially addressing the pervasive issue of inequalities in access to healthcare and resources, but also driving differences in the ageing process.
Our proposal emphasises capacity building, not only in terms of research skills but also in addressing inequalities. Combining the diverse expertise of both countries, we can develop skills and knowledge that benefit future generations. Both countries offer unique insights into addressing health disparities in diverse communities, while contributing cutting-edge research and innovation. We will also fully exploit existing datasets that are available in both countries to assess healthy ageing. This collaboration empowers individuals and institutions with the tools to drive lasting change, fostering greater equity and inclusivity in the process.
The impact of our research extends beyond our immediate communities. By enhancing healthy ageing and addressing inequalities among older people, we can promote economic productivity and social cohesion. Our collaborative approach fosters international cooperation, leading to valuable experience and knowledge exchange. These efforts will benefit societies globally while identifying deep-rooted inequalities driving unhealthy ageing. In summary, our network will bridge nations and seeks to create a brighter, healthier, and more equitable future for older adults.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Empowering Environmental Health and Wellbeing through Interdisciplinary Advancements in Sustainable Multi-Sensor Platforms with Energy Harvesting
descriptions:
Malaysia is blessed with many natural beauty and resources but continuous urbanisation and economic activities from manufacturing, agriculture, mining and construction [1] generated many wastes that cause environmental health issues, including the management of infectious diseases, chemical poisoning, and air and water quality [2,3]. Public health research has taken significant steps forward by leveraging the potential of multi-modal sensing systems, which use various technologies to collect data on location, environmental conditions, public health, and biophysical factors. This data aids in the proactive prevention of diseases while creating environments that support good health.
For the past decade, research has been focused on the integration of wireless sensing devices with artificial intelligence algorithms. This approach has been implemented in smart, sustainable cities and healthcare projects in Malaysia. However, its true potential for efficiency can only be fully realised by implementing energy harvesting methods to ensure long-term sustainability.
The transition from conventional batteries to more sustainable energy sources is paramount for the widespread adoption of sensing systems globally. This research isn't just about cutting-edge technology; it's about significantly improving people's lives. It can lead to cleaner air, reduced disease rates, and safer cities, contributing to a better world for all.
In pursuit of this goal, a new partnership, supported by this grant, will be established with energy harvesting experts from the University of Exeter (UoE). Only with the complementary expertise and interdisciplinary collaboration between Universiti Malaysia Perlis and UoE that an energy-self-sufficient sensing platform for Environmental Health and Wellbeing can be realised.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Development of a DMPK network in Brazil
descriptions:
Drug metabolism and pharmacokinetics (DMPK) is an essential part of the drug discovery process, providing data on properties vital for the development of new compounds (1).  While Brazil has a large academic drug discovery community (2), they are lacking the facilities to perform these DMPK experiments.  Currently academics have to send their samples to overseas companies, incurring additional time and costs.  
The Wellcome Centre for Anti-Infectives Research at the University of Dundee [WCAIR, (3)] has partnered with a number of institutions in Brazil on drug discovery projects for neglected tropical diseases.  The Brazilian academics have acknowledged that the lack of DMPK in country does limit their capabilities.  A number of institutions have shown a desire to develop this capability in Brazil, but development will be an expensive endeavour.  To ensure that any development is sustainable the entire community needs to engage.
This workshop aims to bring together academics and institutions currently working in drug discovery to discuss their requirements and facilitate the development of network of scientists interested in DMPK.
The proposal is a 2 day workshop, to be held in Sao Paulo state. One day will include up to 50 scientists working in drug discovery who may use future local DMPK facilities, and a second day to bring together groups who have already shown an interest in hosting these facilities.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Circular plastic economy: Bridging theory and practice to train future leaders in sustainable plastics research
descriptions: The global challenge posed by plastics pollution is driving an urgent need to find lasting solutions that address the multiple environmental, economic, political and social drivers of the problem. This project will support a bespoke set of networking and brainstorming activities, leveraging currently funded complementary research in Indonesia and Thailand, in the key areas of plastic pollution prevention, management and environmental leadership development, to co-create a high-level multi-disciplinary training programme for students, researchers and practitioners, in academia, industry, government and civil society; to provide hands-on training in mapping, monitoring, evaluation and modelling of plastics production, consumption and management; to foster leadership in plastics research and innovation, supporting the research needs of the forthcoming Global Plastics Treaty. The activities of the proposed networking programme will facilitate transdisciplinary dialogues, mutual learning, and knowledge co-production between leading plastics researchers and innovators,  of the Plastics in Societies PISCES (www.piscespartnership.org),  Polyurethane foam upcycling (https://ait.ac.th/project/circular-system-innovation-for-polyurethane-foam-catalytic-approach-to-upcycle-foam-waste-from-waste-from-mattresses-beyond/) and Marine Plastics Abatement (MPA, https://ait.ac.th/program/marine-plastics-abatement/) programmes, to co-create a learning environment that encourages and accelerates innovation to ensure challenges along the entire plastics lifecycle are addressed. The training programme will take the form of a Summer School and will be drawing on the expertise of the network participants. By bringing together theory with practice through a multidisciplinary lens, we aim to form the first multi-regional, multi-dimensional, multi-disciplinary and multi-stakeholder Summer School to solely focus on the challenge of plastic pollution prevention, supporting sustainable innovation in the plastics value.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Ionic Liquids for Sustainable Microalgal Production
descriptions:
"Ionic Liquids for Microalgal Production" is a collaborative endeavor to harness the remarkable potential of microalgae to address some of the world's most pressing challenges. Microalgae are a promising solution for addressing challenges such as climate change, food security, and sustainable energy, as they provide a renewable source of materials that, at the same time, take CO2 from the atmosphere. This project's significance lies in its potential to revolutionize microalgal production using innovative and sustainable approaches.
In this project, the UK researcher will provide invaluable expertise to the ODA collaborators in Indonesia and Malaysia. Through workshops and networking activities, we will explore the use of greener solvents, specifically ionic liquids, in microalgal production. This approach is not only environmentally friendly but also holds the potential to improve the efficiency and sustainability of microalgal cultivation.
Furthermore, the project will delve into the Internet of Things (IoT), which enables real-time monitoring and control of environmental conditions crucial for microalgae growth. Through the networking activities, we will also examine various separation processes, ensuring efficient and sustainable resource utilisation. Additionally, mathematical modeling will play a significant role in our exploration.
The impact of our research extends far beyond the laboratory. It offers the promise of a greener, more sustainable future, reducing our carbon footprint and increasing access to nutritious food and clean energy. By combining the expertise of our international collaborators and innovative approaches, our networking proposal holds the potential to bring about meaningful change for the benefit of society as a whole.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: AI-ECG: applications of artificial intelligence to the electrocardiogram
descriptions:
This project focuses on using artificial intelligence (AI) to address cardiovascular diseases (CVD), a leading cause of global mortality. The project's core revolves around using AI methods to obtain diagnostic and predictive information from standard 12-lead electrocardiograms (ECGs), a widely availabel and low-cost method.
The Federal University of Minas Gerais (UFMG) in Brazil is pivotal in this initiative. UFMG has curated a database of 2.4 million ECGs, enriched with comprehensive health data, led by Prof Antonio Luiz Ribeiro (Lead applicant). Using AI technology, Ribeiro and colleagues have developed an AI system that outperforms many healthcare professionals and students in identifying six specific categories of cardiac anomalies.
In collaboration with the UFMG team, experts from Imperial College London (Co-applicants: Fu Siong Ng, Arunashis Sau) have enhanced the AI model, improving its accuracy in predicting heart conditions and premature mortality. Imperial College London's world-leading AI expertise is vital to the project's success.
This collaboration will extend beyond AI model development, aiming for practical implementation in the UK and Brazil. This includes early identification of health risks and preventive measures to enhance health outcomes. The fundamental mission is to bridge healthcare disparities, ensuring equitable access to healthcare, irrespective of geographical location.
Planned activities involve bilateral visits, seminars, workshops, and virtual meetings to facilitate knowledge exchange and collaboration between the UFMG and Imperial College London teams. In essence, this initiative represents a significant step toward enhancing cardiovascular health and advancing global public health and well-being.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Mental health literacy for secondary school learners: Building capacity through the Pan-African Mental Health Research Network (PAMHRN)
descriptions: Good mental health starts in childhood, with the majority of problems having onset during the school years (REF1). If not recognised, mental health problems can lead to a child’s decreased physical, cognitive, and social functioning, and lower academic achievement (REF2). Mental health literacy is important for promoting good mental health in schoolchildren. Research evidence indicates that mental health literacy in schoolchildren can promote good mental health as it helps recognise the need to seek professional health for themselves or their peers (REF3). This may in turn contribute to eliminating negative attitudes and stigma toward mental health problems (REF4). Unfortunately, most of what we know about mental health literacy comes from studies conducted in high-income countries. A recent systematic review protocol suggests that mental health literacy in youth in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) has received less research attention (REF5). We aim to develop a network of mental health specialists with complementary expertise across different disciplines (i.e., psychology, education, psychiatry, public health, and social work) from several SSA countries - South Africa, Kenya, Malawi, Uganda, Nigeria, and Zimbabwe, as well as from the UK and Jamaica. We will provide research training to 20 early career researchers (ECRs) from these countries. In consultations with the Youth Advisory Group (YAG), we will co-design a study to investigate mental health literacy views and needs among secondary schoolchildren in Limpopo Province (South Africa). We will use these data to apply for a large collaborative grant to design a mental health literacy intervention for SSA schoolchildren.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Innovation in recycling organic wastes for low-cost and labour-efficient soil improvement in South Asia
descriptions: Village surveys conducted in South Asia have indicated that low-income farmers often lack financial resources or access to markets to purchase synthetic fertilisers. However, they also waste significant quantities of nitrogen by allowing organic wastes to be lost, especially from animal housing. Due to recent increases in the cost of fertilisers, more farmers than ever before are finding they cannot access or afford synthetic fertilisers. Therefore, making good use of organic wastes that are available on their farms is increasingly important to maintaining and enhancing food production. Sustainable uptake of increased recycling of organic wastes to the soil requires innovations that are both low-cost and labour-efficient, while also providing alternatives for competing uses of organic wastes, for example for household energy or as building materials. This subject area builds on previous work by the lead applicant that developed new methods to reduce nitrogen waste from livestock systems. The proposed work will bring together scientists from across Bangladesh, Nepal and the UK to discuss methods of recycling organic wastes to reduce loss of nutrients and increase the organic matter content of the soil. Loss of organic wastes from farming systems has a wider environment and societal impact because excess reactive nitrogen has an adverse impact on air and water quality. Furthermore, effective recycling of organic wastes to the soil not only improves productivity, but also sequesters carbon, so reducing emissions of greenhouse gases. Therefore, the proposed project is both timely and important to the farmers and populations of Bangladesh and Nepal.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: A Roadmap for Building with Nature for Climate Change Adaptation: A Framework based on Place-Based Case Studies
descriptions:
The consequences of climate change include droughts and water scarcity, wildfires, melting polar ice, sea level rise, flooding, catastrophic storms and declining biodiversity with risks to communities and infrastructure (United Nations 2022). Urgent far-reaching action is needed to avoid the worst consequences of climate change. 
Climate change puts coastal communities at risk of flooding and coastal erosion due to more frequent and intense storms on top of sea level rise. There are various cited climate change mitigation policies (reducing greenhouse gas emissions) and various climate adaptation policies  (adjusting to the inevitable effects of climate change). While hard-engineered coastal defences are costly to build and maintain, living coastal defences such as oyster reefs are self-sustaining and can grow with sea level rise.
With collaboration between higher education, local government, local businesses, and the local community, there is potential to build a circular economy around waste oyster shells from local restaurants to seed living oyster reefs that defend the coastline. To achieve a road-map for the various challenges to consider in the implementation of a circular economy around waste oyster shells, we will conduct a comparative pilot case study analysis using a place-based approach (UK, Thailand, Egypt). The pilot comparative case studies will be based on place-based approach where a collection of pilot data and knowledge exchange between the network collaborators been conducted. This work will have important benefits to communities in Thailand.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Bridging indigenous knowledge with modern techniques: A Collaborative Approach for Sustainable Dyes in Northern Vietnam
descriptions:
The integration of indigenous knowledge into modern practice has emerged as a promising approach in various fields, including sustainable natural resource management. Our collaboration aims to work closely with ethnic communities in the mountainous region in Northern Vietnam to combine traditional knowledge of plant-based colorants with modern scientific techniques in the textile industry to facilitate a sustainable and culturally significant approach to dyeing, specifically:
(1)  Cultural heritage and indigenous knowledge preservation
Recording, recognizing and utilizing indigenous knowledge acknowledges its value and empowers indigenous communities. It helps preserve traditional practices, customs, and knowledge systems that are integral to their identities. This is important as this trove of knowledge are vulnerable against industrialisation and urbanisation because of factors such as high labor costs or decline in market of traditional products that use plant dye.
(2) Sustainable and innovative Practices: 
While ethnobotanists' expertise in traditional knowledge can help identify sustainable dyeing techniques that are less harmful to the environment, modern techniques can be used to optimize traditional dyeing methods. Combining modern dyeing techniques with traditional knowledge can lead to innovation in the field of textile dyeing.
(3) Cross-Cultural Learning: 
The Project facilitates cross-cultural learning and understanding, and the exchange of ideas, perspectives, and experiences. This mutual learning can foster a deeper appreciation for diverse worldviews. The UK has a long history of textile production and dyeing, and sharing this knowledge with indigenous communities can lead to a better understanding of each other's cultures.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: An interdisciplinary research network for dementia: Paving the way to transform prevention and timely diagnosis for dementia in Malaysia
descriptions: Over 300,000 people aged over 60 years in Malaysia are estimated to be living with dementia. This number will reach half a million by 2040. Yet, Malaysia does not have a dementia plan. While dementia research is gaining momentum, the picture on dementia prevention and timely diagnosis is patchy and under-researched. We will establish a dementia network to bring together dementia researchers, workers, and organisations from different parts of the country, and set up a Patient and Public Involvement group. This will allow us to share resources and identify research that matter most to affected individuals and families. We know that dementia awareness and knowledge among both medical professionals and the public is low. As a result, dementia is often misconceived either as part of the normal ageing process or as a stigmatised condition. However, we know little of the challenges that people are facing in seeking help or navigating the heath system for a dementia diagnosis. We will record stories of lived experience of help-seeking and health system navigation with people with dementia, carers, and families. We will share these stories on our network website to raise awareness of dementia and with stakeholders in a workshop to produce a list of prioritized research areas. Our work would lead to an improved dementia awareness and knowledge, better help-seeking experience and navigation for a timely diagnosis.  In the long run,  affected families will bear lesser economic and care-giving burden, and treatment cost and stress placed on the healthcare systems will reduce.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Empowering Healthcare with Automated Analysis: Addressing the Surge in Medical Data Through Collaboration and Innovation
descriptions:
The exponential growth of medical data from laboratories and hospitals worldwide has created a significant burden on healthcare professionals. With a shortage of experts capable of analyzing this vast dataset, there's an urgent demand for the automation of data analysis processes. Prominent examples of this necessity include the analysis of comet assay images and the accurate segmentation of cancer cells via plasma membrane recognition.

Comet assay, a widely employed technique for evaluating DNA damage and repair in individual cells, plays a pivotal role in genetic damage assessment and human biomonitoring within medical and biological research. However, detecting cellular injury and recovery in comet assay images remains a daunting challenge. Likewise, the precise identification and classification of cancer cells represent ongoing research obstacles.

This proposal primarily focuses on fostering collaboration among data-collecting specialists in laboratories, image processing experts, and machine learning researchers. The goal is to harness their collective expertise to develop cutting-edge automated image-processing techniques. Through network meetings, the researchers will work on how to empower accurate detection, annotation, and segmentation of images obtained in laboratory settings. By bridging the gap between domain-specific knowledge and advanced computational methodologies, we aspire to enhance medical data analysis, thereby advancing healthcare and scientific research.

Crucially, this work will benefit communities in Indonesia, Turkey, and Malaysia.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Capacity Building and Computing Technologies for Healthcare: An Application in Transforming Mental Health Research and Services in Vietnam
descriptions:
Healthcare technologies are rapidly advancing and will revolutionise the provision of healthcare. For example, wearable devices and digital health apps enable remote monitoring, virtual diagnosis and care; artificial intelligence leads to improvements in personalised medicine, diagnosis and treatment outcomes.  The overall aim of this proposal is to establish a healthcare technology network between the UK and Vietnam, ensuring Vietnam is positioned to leverage on these innovative technologies and enable rapid advancement of its healthcare system.
The project entails building a collaborative network between an internationally leading Computer Science Department in the UK, which is developing cutting-edge Healthcare Technologies, and a top Biomedical Engineering Department in Vietnam. This provides the foundations for establishing a UK-Vietnam-Southeast Asia consortium on healthcare technology research tailored to the needs and constraints of local healthcare systems.
We will initially prioritise our focus on mental illness, an increasingly common condition plagued by stigma, poor diagnosis, and lack of available treatment options. As a catalyst to establishing our network, we will embark on a collaborative pilot project that will adapt state-of-the-art healthcare activity monitoring technology for successful deployment in Vietnam; this will involve adapting activity monitoring algorithms to local cultural and environmental differences. The technology will initially be applied to healthy subjects with age-stratification before being applied to clinical cohorts, patients with depression; thus, assisting with diagnosis, monitoring of health conditions and response to treatment. Most importantly, it can be deployed at scale, with low-cost and in remote settings, offering significant potential for improving healthcare in developing countries.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Developing a BIM-based Immersive Learning Environment for Enhanced Construction Management Education and Training using VR Technology (DOMINEERING)
descriptions: There are over 20,000 students/leaners on construction related courses in technical/higher education in Vietnam. The graduates assist investors/contractors to make decisions in construction projects and on sites, therefore, their skills and knowledge will surely have great impact on the project success. Thousands of practitioners continue taking courses for career development. For the course quality assurance, students should be trained in the context of real construction projects. This is especially significant for quality and safety management, two of the core domains in construction management. However, this requirement is hardly addressed successfully due to the complexity, costs and risk in bringing learners to sites. Disruptive digital technologies such as BIM and Virtual Reality (VR) can facilitate this requirement. VR technology enables students to explore and interact with realistic BIM-based safety and quality management scenarios. With building projects visualized, students can immerse themselves in real construction sites to identify unsafe zones/activities. Students can also virtually inspect and review construction progress in real-time to identify defects, deviations, and clashes against the design. Over the past decade, several UK universities have introduced various construction management programs with a focus on BIM and VR to foster informed decision-making skills among students. This project aims to develop a BIM-based immersive learning platform for construction management training and education in Vietnam, using lessons learnt and exploiting expertise from the UK through networking events and activities. The project can provide universities with a disruptive learning solution, which can also be adopted by businesses for upskilling the human resources.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Establishing a Thailand-UK partnership on the production of innovative bioproducts from microbial bioresources and fungal platforms
descriptions: Southeast Asia boasts a rich diversity of microorganisms, with the Thailand Bioresource Research Center (TBRC) of the National Center for Genetic Engineering and Biotechnology (BIOTEC) standing as the largest regional repository of microbial cultures. TBRC also has networking with many microbial culture collections e.g. the InaCC of Indonesia and the PNCM of Philippines. One of BIOTEC's endeavors is dedicated to exploring the potential of microorganisms particularly diverse fungi for production of fuels, chemical, pharmaceuticals, food ingredients, and value-added products from inexpensive biomass, aligning with the Bio-Circular-Green Economy. BIOTEC is keen on developing fungal platforms for their use as cell factories. The Kent Fungal Group (KFG) of the University of Kent is the UK's leader in fungal studies. KFG's research employs interdisciplinary technologies, particularly computational models and multi-omic approaches, to investigate biological processes of fungi and contribute to the development of recombinant proteins and innovative food sources by fungal platforms. The formation of the Thailand-UK partnership holds the potential to accelerate the development of new and IP-free fungal platforms, empowering us to engage in impactful research. Within this proposal, we delineate the activities, starting with a kick-off meeting at the KFG where potential research collaborations will be discussed. Moreover, we will arrange a comprehensive two-week training program related to the development of fungal platforms, offering this opportunity to BIOTEC researchers in the KFG laboratory. Additionally, we will arrange an international workshop on microbial resources and fungal platforms in Thailand to disseminate knowledge among participants and speakers and develop the networking consortium. Moreover, this work will benefit communities in Myanmar, Viet Nam, Indonesia, Thailand, Philippines, and Malaysia.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Clinical Research capacity evidence gathering
descriptions: This project will explore clinical research pathways in ODA eligible countries to understand the pipeline for clinical researchers in each country; identify key stages in the development pathway to support clinical researchers; provide ideas for further improving and target key stages in the career pathway to ensure diverse researchers continue on and contribute to excellent clinical research.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Clinical Research capacity scoping activities
descriptions: Scoping activities to inform the development of the clinical research pathways project. This will formulate final aims, objectives and structure of the project before evidence gathering and delivery.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Crises in the Horn of Africa: Transforming research for policy makers into an international research profile
descriptions: This project brings together scholars with experience of translating policy-oriented research for academic and broader policy and public audiences and editorial experience with early career researchers (ECRs) from the Horn of Africa (Djibouti, Ethiopia, Eritrea, Kenya, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, and Uganda) involved in policy-oriented projects on regional crises. ECRs will be trained in and supported to translate research conducted into an article in a leading peer reviewed academic journal, will be trained in grant application writing and will be supported to submit a funding application. This project targets the following SDGs: Reduced Inequality; Decent Work and Economic Growth; Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Transforming research capacity for female early career researchers in Jordan
descriptions:
This project responds to the challenges of publishing in high impact journals and achieving global reach experienced by female early career researchers (ECRs) in Jordan, which include low female representation in academia, institutional, scientific and societal barriers and Global North expectations which sideline research from Jordan and the Global South. 

The project aims to transform female Jordanian ECRs publication pathways and broader career development through a a co-designed skills-building programme that scaffolds sustainable international collaborations and the development of a gender-inclusive research and innovation infrastructure.

This project targets the following SDGs: Reduced Inequality; Gender Equality; Decent Work and Economic Growth.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Human Rights Education and Activism in South-East Asia: Developing the Publication and Grant-writing Capacity of ECR Scholar-Activists in Challenging
descriptions: This project will develop the capacity of 24 early career researcher ‘scholar-activists’ in the fields of human rights education and activism in South-East Asia (SEA) to write for publication, to successfully apply for research funding and to cascade this learning to other scholar-activists.  The countries that will benefit from this project are Thailand, Philippines, Vietnam, Indonesia and Malaysia.  This project targets the following SDGs: Reduced Inequality; Decent Work and Economic Growth; Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Senegal International Writing Workshop for Francophone West and Central African ECRs
descriptions:
This project offers a robust, long-term, and collaboratively-designed programme aimed at training and mentoring French-speaking West and Central African early career researchers (ECRs), with a focus on journalism, media, and conflict studies in Africa. 

The project brings together 25 early career researchers (ECRs) and 10 internationally-recognised academics for a 5-day intensive workshop in Senegal. The workshop will directly address the challenges faced by Francophone African scholars, such as limited access to higher education and the standards expected by high-impact journals, thus contributing to tackling the issue of Western frameworks dominating the presentation of African realities.

The countries that will directly benefit from this project are Senegal, Burkino Faso, Niger, Mali and the Democratic Republic of the Congo.  This project targets the following SDGs: Reduced Inequality; Decent Work and Economic Growth; Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Advancing Research on International Politics in Africa: A Training and Networking Initiative
descriptions: The project will bring together Africa-based international relations scholars to exchange ideas and expertise and contribute to this growing body of research on Africa’s international relations.The project will consist of three main activities: 1) a paper-presentation workshop, where all participants will present draft papers submitted prior to the workshop and receive feedback from their peers and editors of African politics journals; 2) a methodology workshop, covering themes related to the methods participants will employ in their draft papers; and 3) a publishing workshop, led by editors of some of the most influential journals in African politics, offering guidance on how to publish in these top outlets.  In addition to enabling participants to network and form potential collaborations, the project’s key outcomes will include the publication of draft papers in a special issue of a leading African politics journal, as well as improved knowledge of academic writing and methodological approaches. The countries that will directly benefit from this project are Kenya, United Republic of Tanzania and South Africa.This project targets the following SDGs: Reduced Inequality; Decent Work and Economic Growth; Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Elevate Jordan: A Three-Day Writing Workshop and Year-Long Mentoring Programme to Build Research Capacity for Early Career Researchers in Jordan
descriptions: Despite increased higher education enrolment in Jordan, economic growth remains stagnant. This highlights an urgent need for investment in early career researchers (ECRs). Project “Elevate Jordan” will recruit 30 Jordanian ECRs for a three-day workshop and year-long mentoring program to develop their research capacity. Objectives include enhancing knowledge of manuscript publishing, providing expert guidance in academic writing, providing high-quality personalised guidance and mentorship, and supporting networking opportunities. The project targets ECRs in the humanities, health, and social sciences and promotes diversity and inclusion. The project directly aligns with program aims by supporting ECRs in a developing country, fostering professional networks, and enhancing capacity through international collaboration. This project targets the following SDGs: Reduced Inequality; Decent Work and Economic Growth; Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Bridging Research to Publication: Advanced Writing Workshops for Jordanian Early Career Researchers
descriptions:
Academic writing and publishing are critical gaps in the research system across the Levant, as the current focus is on coursework and teaching rather than research outputs, leaving researchers underprepared for international publication.  This project aims to overcome these challenges through a series of workshops and dedicated mentoring scheme delivered to the Jordanian early career academic community by local and international experts.

Through the project, participants will be equipped with the necessary knowledge and skills to publish in international journals, thereby developing their research potential and fostering professional growth. In addition to which, the project will facilitate professional networks that connect early career researchers with national and international academics, ultimately increasing the visibility and impact of research from developing regions.

This project targets the following SDGs: Reduced Inequality; Decent Work and Economic Growth; Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Innovative Approaches to Justice in Brazil: An Inclusive Writing Workshop Series
descriptions: This project empowers early-career researchers by enhancing academic writing skills, fostering interdisciplinary and international networks, and amplifying marginalised voices in justice scholarship. It addresses critical issues, including high incarceration rates, institutional violence, social inequalities, and environmental injustice linked to deforestation, resource exploitation, and Indigenous marginalisation. This project targets the following SDGs: Reduced Inequality; Decent Work and Economic Growth; Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Advancing Southeast-Asian Psychology In Research Excellence
descriptions: Focusing on the underrepresentation of scholars from Southeast Asia in top psychology journals, the workshops will cover academic writing, peer review, and grant applications. Participants will write and submit a first-authored paper, receive 1-to-1 mentorship, engage with journal editors, collaborate on grant proposals, and engage in regional and global networking.The long-term goal is to increase research output and visibility of Southeast Asian psychologists, contributing to a more inclusive and globalized psychology field. The countries that will benefit directly from this project are Thailand, Myanmar, Cambodia and Lao People’s Democratic Republic.This project targets the following SDGs: Reduced Inequality; Decent Work and Economic Growth; Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Strengthening Early-Career Researchers to Drive Thailand’s Knowledge Economy Forward
descriptions: This project will support early-career researchers in the social sciences. The programme will offer skills training, tailored mentorship, and strategies for publishing in high-impact journals. By the end of the workshop, participants will: 1) better understand the publication process and feel confident in submitting articles to international journals; 2) develop skills to identify and apply for international research funding; and 3) establish meaningful connections with leading academics. The proposed workshop aims to address the immediate hurdles faced by early-career researchers and position them as key contributors to Thailand's transformation into a knowledge-driven economy. Through training in cross-disciplinary research, global collaboration, and strategic publishing, the workshop is expected to generate a cascading impact, strengthening the nation’s broader research landscape. Additionally, its inclusive focus on the social sciences ensures a comprehensive strategy, empowering researchers to tackle Thailand’s socio-economic challenges while advancing its global standing under the Thailand 4.0 initiative. This project targets the following SDGs: Reduced Inequality; Decent Work and Economic Growth; Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Writing southern urbanism(s): Addressing publishing challenges for emergent voices in Urban studies in Brazil and South Africa
descriptions: The project will provide a comprehensive support system, including mentorship, training, and networking opportunities, to enhance early career researchers'  (ECRs') writing skills for publishing research articles, book chapters, grants and policy briefs with experienced journal editors and policymakers.Key activities include three online interactive sessions on research capacity development and a continuing mentorship scheme for two years, two 3-day writing workshops in Cape Town, South Africa and Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, and one conclusive hybrid session on shaping southern epistemic communities. This project targets the following SDGs: Reduced Inequality; Gender Equality; Decent Work and Economic Growth.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Gender, Equity and Curriculum: A training and mentorship program for Uganda's early career researchers’ writing skills for research, grant application
descriptions:
The scarcity of high-quality publications in academic research, curriculum, and education has posed significant challenges for Uganda in addressing gender equality and poverty reduction. In response, this project focuses on developing the gender-and-equity curriculum focussed writing skills of early career researchers and curriculum specialists. 

Through a series of workshops, the project will focus on developing writing skills for research and publications, grant applications and curriculums. fter the workshops, high-quality manuscripts will be published in international and local journals, curriculums with international standard will be written for local schools and collaborative grant applications will be drafted. 

This project targets the following SDGs: Reduced Inequality;  Quality Education; Decent Work and Gender Equality.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Writing Workshops in Brazil
descriptions: Through a series of workshops in Brazil, early career researchers (ECRs) will be equipped with enhanced skills in academic writing, peer reviewing, and preparing grant applications. This includes the development of draft articles ready for submission to high-impact journals. The project aims to increase the visibility of research from Brazil, and to encourage multilingual strategies to ensure that diverse knowledge is included. The country that will benefit directly from this project is Brazil. This project targets the following SDGs: Reduced Inequality; Decent Work and Economic Growth; Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Amplifying Sub-Saharan African Climate Adaptation Research: Bridging the Epistemic Gap and Promoting Global Visibility
descriptions: Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) is struggling to adapt to climate change impacts, such as droughts. However, SSA climate change researchers are acutely underrepresented in science publications, hence have low influence in international debates. This is also a justice issue, because SSA has fewer opportunities to justify and showcase their science-based and indigenous knowledge solutions.This project will support early-career SSA researchers in improving their writing and publishing skills and will contribute to the representation and visibility of early-career SSA researchers in global climate science and policy debates. It will help achieve climate justice by promoting equity, diversity and inclusion of locally produced knowledge in global climate solutions.The countries that will benefit from this project are South Africa and Kenya. This project targets the following SDGs: Reduced Inequality; Climate Action; Decent Work and Economic Growth.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: The Fourth Industrial Revolution and Agricultural Transformation in South Africa
descriptions: This workshop, themed "The Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR) and Agricultural Transformation in South Africa," seeks to empower early-career researchers (ECRs) to produce high-quality, context-specific academic publications. Agriculture remains vital to South Africa’s economy and food security, but it faces challenges such as climate change and limited adoption of modern technologies. This project targets the following SDGs: Reduced Inequality; Responsible Consumption and Production; Decent Work and Economic Growth.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Enhancing Writing Skills and Building Academic Networks: Supporting Career Development of Early Career Social Science Researchers in Indonesia
descriptions: The project will bring together 15 early career social science researchers across Indonesia working on issues of social inequalities and exclusion. Social Science early career researchers (ECRs) in Indonesia face significant challenges in getting their work published in international peer-reviewed journals and securing grants and so, through the workshops, participants will receive hands-on training and one-to-one feedback to develop a paper and will also receive information and support to develop funding bids for both national and international funders. At the community level, the programme will strengthen the research culture by setting higher standards for academic writing and promoting ethical publication practices. Beyond academia, the published work will contribute  to policy and practice, addressing critical societal issues such as inequality, education reform, and cultural preservation. In the long term, these initiatives align with Indonesia’s ‘Golden Vision for 2045’ by fostering a resilient and resourceful scholarly community as well as evidence-based policy cultivated through research activities. This project targets the following SDGs: Reduced Inequality; Gender Equality; Decent Work and Economic Growth.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: South African Voices in the Arts and Social Sciences
descriptions: This project brings together a diverse cohort of early career researchers with internationally successful academics and journal editors from South Africa and the UK. This collaboration will empower South African researchers to build international publishing careers in high-impact journals, while simultaneously championing their unique perspectives and approaches.The importance of this project lies in its dual focus: fostering authentic academic voices from South Africa and providing comprehensive career mentoring and development, contributing to the development of the higher education sector and broader civic and economic development. This project targets the following SDGs: Reduced Inequality; Decent Work and Economic Growth; Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Advancing the social sciences in Kenya: an international writing skills workshop and mentoring scheme for future research leaders
descriptions:
The proposed two-year project aims to support Kenya to become internationally renowned for excellence across three key social science disciplines: health, business and education. It will select 20 emerging early career social scientists across three Kenyan Universities/Research Institutes to participate in an in-person academic writing workshop in Nairobi, and to receive two-year online group mentoring from senior UK social scientists. 

Through this project, Kenyan early career social scientists will gain: hands-on experience to improve their academic paper/grant writing; first-hand knowledge of journal submission processes; and new scholarly networks. They will also help create a supportive academic writing culture at their home institutions, with peer writing groups and training. Through successfully delivering these activities, the project will support creation of the next generation of global leaders in social sciences.

This project targets the following SDGs: Reduced Inequality; Decent Work and Economic Growth; Quality Education.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Researching, Writing and Publishing on Gender, Culture and Society: Upskilling Early Career Researchers (ECRs) in Türkiye
