descriptions: This programme targets Early Career Researchers (ECRs) from universities across Türkiye working in interdisciplinary gender studies. Each participant will be supported to write a publishable journal article in English. Participants will attend in-person workshops where they will gain insight into writing for publication and applying for grants with editors of leading journals and publishers of academic monographs. This project targets the following SDGs: Reduced Inequality; Gender Equality; Decent Work and Economic Growth.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: British Academy Brazil Academic Writing Workshops in Philosophy and Law
descriptions: This project includes a series of four three-day workshops focused on early-career researchers in Philosophy and Law in Brazil. Workshops participants will receive tailored feedback and one-to-one mentoring on a specific piece of career-development work, such as a journal article or grant application. The workshops will also provide advice on a range of career-development topics (including article publication, grant application, job application) with a view to equalising opportunities for success in two competitive academic disciplines in which Brazilian researchers face disadvantage.This project targets the following SDGs:  Reduced Inequality; Decent Work and Economic Growth; Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Building Research Capacity through Writing: A Workshop for Researchers in African Countries
descriptions:
This project will provide early career researchers with mentorship from journal editors and senior academic researchers from Africa and internationally, through which they will gain strategic support to amplify their own research and to provide peer-to-peer support to colleagues. 

By convening researchers and facilitators from the Global South and the Global North, the project aims to allow for rich dialogues on relevant experiences of writing, publishing and applying for research grants regionally and internationally, leading to democratisation and co-constructing knowledge about the dynamics of international publications. It will also help journal editors to understand the barriers that African researchers face, and how these can best be supported by them. Consequently, the participants will be empowered to disseminate their research internationally and thus increase the potential of contributing to global academic debates.

This project will directly benefit Kenya and Uganda. 

The project targets the following SDGs: Reduced Inequality; Decent Work and Economic Growth; Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Considering Just Urban Transitions in African cities
descriptions: The project focuses on how emerging scholars are studying, theorising, and exploring the ways that African cities are driving towards Just Urban Transitions. Through a collaboration between Global North and South Higher Education Institutions (HEIs), think-tanks, and journals, the partners and participants will co-produce sustained online and in person engagements to enhance African scholars' capacity for publication in high-impact journals and provide guidance on promoting their work on other platforms to ensure the greatest impact. This project will directly benefit South Africa. This project targets the following SDGs: Reduced Inequality; Decent Work and Economic Growth; Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Research and writing in building African agency: The role of non-state actors in global governance of the environment and socio-economic development
descriptions:
This workshop series will provide a platform for early career researchers (ECRs) from the Humanities and Social Sciences in South Africa to develop research, writing and networking skills through the preparation of a research paper for publication.
Through workshops and one-to-one mentoring, early career researchers will be supported in writing, publication, understanding external research grant capture, and enhancing the visibility and impact of research. 

As part of the project, participants will be guided in developing their own research project on the theme of African non-state actors and global governance, for which they will be encouraged to link their planned research to the following sustainable development goals: Reduced Inequality; Partnerships to achieve the Goals; No Poverty; Gender Equality; Climate Action.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Promoting local perspectives on the political and security crises in the Sahel neighbourhood: A mentoring programme for early career political scienti
descriptions: The programme will strengthen the participants’ academic writing and research funding application skills, establish a supportive cross-national network of scholars working on political and security dynamics, and lead to the publication on original articles by authors from the region in internationally recognised journals. As such, it will contribute to supporting the career-progression of promising early-career scholars, while increasing the uptake of research by African scholars on African issues by scholars and policymakers globally. The countries that will directly benefit from this project are Burkino Faso, Senegal, Niger, Mali and Benin. This project targets the following SDGs: Reduced Inequality; Decent Work and Economic Growth; Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Advancing Innovation and Sustainability Research
descriptions:
Southeast Asia is a region of immense opportunity yet faces significant challenges. Rapid urbanisation, industrialisation, and population growth have spurred economic development in countries such as Myanmar, Laos, Cambodia, Malaysia, Thailand, and Vietnam. However, these forces have also intensified environmental degradation, widened social inequalities, and created complex demographic shifts. Despite these pressing issues, the region often struggles with limited research capacity, hindering its ability to publish in international peer-reviewed journals and contribute effectively to global discourses.

To address these challenges, this project will build the capacity of early career researchers (ECRs) to produce high-quality research and secure funding in the fields of innovation and sustainability. By equipping ECRs with the skills to publish in international peer-reviewed journals, the project enhances the visibility and impact of Southeast Asia’s contributions to global sustainability goals and fosters actionable solutions to the region’s complex and interrelated issues. This project targets the following SDGs:  Reduced Inequality; Decent Work and Economic Growth; Sustainable Cities and Communities.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Empowering future generations of Malaysian social scientists: Writing skills and research design capacity for early-career researchers.
descriptions:
This programme aims to train early-career researchers (ECRs) from Malaysia in writing and publishing skills and to improve funding success in social sciences research. This is motivated by the underrepresentation of Malaysian scholars in social sciences research. The key themes of the workshops are: a) manuscript writing for scientific publication, b) securing research funding, c) career development, and d) capacity building for Malaysian social science researchers. The workshop outcomes include strengthened publishing skills, improved research capacity, enhanced funding success rates, and the establishment of long-term academic collaborations.
This project targets the following SDGs: Reduced Inequality; Decent Work and Economic Growth; Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Building Research and Publication Capacity of Emerging Scholars in the Mindanao region of Southern Philippines.
descriptions: These workshops build on the research team’s experience of supporting Global South researchers to produce indigenous knowledge and scholarship on post-conflict peacebuilding challenges using a range of data collection methods. The primary aim is to develop the publishing skills of emerging scholars and thereby enrich the visibility of indigenous insider knowledge on peace and conflict studies from the postwar region of Mindanao, in southern Philippines. This project targets the following SDGs: Reduced Inequality; Decent Work and Economic Growth; Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Accessible Quantitative Political Science: A Workshop for Emerging Scholars in Turkey
descriptions: This project will provide 15 early career researchers in Turkey with ongoing mentorship and tailored training to overcome structural challenges that hinder publishing in high-impact journals and securing external funding. Over a two-year period, participants will engage with established scholars and journal editors, gaining insights into best practices in publication processes and grant acquisition. By fostering equitable partnerships, promoting inclusivity, and addressing structural inequalities, this project will enhance the visibility and impact of research emerging from Turkey while connecting early career researchers with global academic networks. This project targets the following SDGs: Reduced Inequality; Decent Work and Economic Growth; Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Participatory research methods: an interdisciplinary writing and mentoring programme for emerging scholars in Turkey
descriptions: This interdisciplinary writing and mentoring programme supports Turkish early career researchers in political science, sociology, art, and educational sciences. This programme includes two in-person workshops and a bespoke mentoring scheme. Participants will develop writing skills, expand research networks, and access funding opportunities. A wider impact will be achieved through dissemination events and “train-the-trainer” seminars, ensuring sustainability and furthering knowledge exchange across academic communities. This project targets the following SDGs: Reduced Inequality; Decent Work and Economic Growth;Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: African Leadership Ethics
descriptions: The project will support early-career researchers in Africa to develop publishable manuscripts on African approaches to leadership ethics. It will bring together 12 early-career researchers with experienced journal editors and scholars for intensive mentorship, culminating in a writing workshop. It combines three key phases: pre-workshop online mentoring, a three-day workshop, and sustained post-workshop support to ensure successful publication outcomes. The countries that will directly benefit from the project are South Africa, Malawi, United Republic of Tanzania, Rwanda, Uganda. This project targets the following SDGs: Reduced Inequality; Decent Work and Economic Growth; Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Capacity Building for Turkey-based Syrian Academics through Collaborative Research Writing: Disseminating and Sustaining Vital Action Research
descriptions:
This project will develop the funding proposal and output writing skills of early-career, Turkey-based Syrian academics through two in-person workshops and a series of online activities.   

Academic mentors will guide the Syrian research teams to disseminate their findings through multiple modalities, and plan for further research to extend and sustain their work, thereby enabling  the participants to contribute to broader debates on the future of Syrian higher education in post-conflict reconstruction. This work is timely, given recent political developments in Syria, and provides a significant opportunity for broad impact across the Syrian higher education sector and post-conflict higher education globally. This project targets the following SDGs: Reduced Inequality; Gender Equality; Decent Work and Economic Growth.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Strengthening Interdisciplinary Global Health Justice Research: Building Publication Capacity in Kenya
descriptions:
This initiative addresses the critical need for enhanced research publication capacity among early-career African researchers working in global health justice. Moving beyond traditional disciplinary boundaries, the program creates a unique platform where scholars from bioethics, philosophy, health systems, and policy sciences converge to develop robust interdisciplinary publication skills. 

The program combines an intensive in-country workshop in Kenya with a comprehensive virtual support system, enhanced by direct access to editorial mentorship through African Journal of Bioethics. This structure maximizes impact while ensuring sustained engagement. Participants will develop practical skills in collaborative research, manuscript development, and grant writing, while building lasting networks for academic success. The focus on global health justice provides a framework for addressing pressing health challenges in Africa while building sustainable research capacity.

The countries that will benefit directly from this project are Kenya, South Africa, Ethiopia, Senegal and Egypt. 

The project targets the following SDGs: Reduced Inequality; Decent Work and Economic Growth; Good Health and Well-Being.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Developing High-impact Research on Language, Culture and Migration: Collaborative Workshops with Women Early Career Researchers in Malaysia.
descriptions:
The project builds on previously developed networks in Malaysia to deliver collaborative writing and mentoring workshops on research publications and grant applications in the intersecting fields of Language, Culture, and Migration.
The programme consists of three main workshops and five mentoring sessions designed to enhance early career researchers’ skills in academic writing, navigating the publishing process, applying for research funding and networking. The ultimate ambition of the programme is to foster a new generation of women researchers in Malaysia who do not face barriers to academic progression and can achieve academic leadership and career success. This project targets the following SDGs: Reduced Inequality; Gender Equality; Decent Work and Economic Growth.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Fostering writing capabilities and networking competence amongst Early Career Researchers in Uganda
descriptions:
This project supports early career researchers (ECRs) in Uganda to develop writing and publishing skills in the fields of sustainable food production and consumer behavioural research. 

The project will involve pre-workshop preparations, physical workshops, virtual webinars, and post-workshop evaluation. 

Outcomes from the series will include increased research publications from Uganda, enhanced ability of participants to secure funding, and the establishment of an enduring research network. Long-term benefits will include a more inclusive and interdisciplinary research culture, contributions to Uganda’s food security solutions, and improved global research visibility. The workshops' focus on sustainability, equity, and capacity-building ensures direct alignment with Uganda’s economic and social development priorities.

This project targets the following SDGs:  Reduced Inequality;Responsible Consumption and Production; Decent Work and Economic Growth.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Writing Mixed-race into Critical Race Discourse: Learnings from Brazil and South Africa
descriptions: Through a series of workshops in Brazil and South Africa, participating  early career scholars will be introduced to the main debates in Critical Mixed Race Studies and will engage with cal and lived experiences of mixed-ness in ex-colonial contexts. By centering discussions on mixed-race identities in the Brazilian and South African contexts, the workshops address a critical gap in understanding racialization and identity formation in post-colonial societies and aim to  generate transformative outcomes and enduring impacts within the fields of Critical Mixed Race Studies, critical race theory, and decolonial scholarship.  The project is expected to bring benefits to Brazil and South Africa by addressing critical gaps in scholarship and fostering transformative engagement with mixed-race identities. This project targets the following SDGs: Reduced Inequality; Decent Work and Economic Growth; Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Enhancing academic writing processes and practice: strengthening academic writing skills in East Africa (Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania).
descriptions:
This project responds to the need to  improve the representation of African scholars as first authors in high-quality international journals. It highlights the barriers academics from  Lower Middle Income Countries face as a result of a lack of funds for journal and library subscription, poor awareness of journal requirements (as a consequence of a lack of exposure to high-impact journals) and inequalities in the publishing industry. 

The project will bring together social science academics and international journal editors to work with early career researchers and established researchers in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda to develop the participants academic writing skills, increase access to high-quality academic writing, and heighten understanding of international journal processes across 24 months of continuous online training and mentorship and through a week-long Writing Workshop in Kenya.

The project will benefit early career researchers, but also more established academics, as it will clearly set out the stages involved in successfully publishing an academic paper, from the research planning stage, through to presentation of research, and will include training on how to select an appropriate journal to submit to, how to draft papers for that journal, the submission process, the peer review process and how to address peer review concerns, and how to navigate article processing charge exemptions for Lower Middle Income Countries. The countries that will directly benefit from this project are Kenya, Uganda and the United Republic of Tanzania. This project targets the following SDGs: Reduced Inequality; Decent Work and Economic Growth; Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Empowering emerging voices: Building research and publication skills in Kurdish Studies
descriptions: These workshops are designed to bring together aspiring scholars in Kurdish Studies in Turkey, enhancing their research and publication skills through collaboration with leading mentors and editors from leading journals in the field. A  deficiency in academic skills and training poses a barrier for these researchers, hindering their active engagement in international debates through the publication of high-quality research in esteemed outlets. Despite their deep knowledge in specific areas, emerging researchers often lack familiarity with publishing in prestigious journals, applying for international grants, or crafting cover letters for job applications that meet international standards. The envisioned workshops aim to address these challenges by assisting researchers in producing papers that adhere to international standards. This project targets the following SDGs: Reduced Inequality; Decent Work and Economic Growth; Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Academic Publishing and Grant Writing Workshop for Early Career Scholars from the Global South working on the nexus between Peace and Conflict Studies
descriptions: This project seeks to strengthen capacities of Early Career Researchers (ECRs) from the Global South as part of the ongoing effort to decolonise knowledge production and encourage South-South and North-South collaborations. Specifically, this project aims to bring together ECRs from two academic fields: Peace and Conflict Studies and Humanitarian Studies, to engage in dialogue and generate new knowledge. The countries that will directly benefit from this project are Brazil and South Africa. This project targets the following SDGs: Reduced Inequality; Decent Work and Economic Growth; Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Strengthening interdisciplinary gender studies in Malaysia: Supporting the research and publication capacity of early career researchers
descriptions:
This programme will strengthen the research and publication capacity of early career gender studies researchers in Malaysia. Using a participatory approach promoting participant involvement and ownership, the programme will create and support an interdisciplinary network of early career scholars who wish to develop an innovative research agenda that speaks to policy, practice and civil society audiences.

The project will consist of three in-person workshops alongside quarterly online research exchange sessions and monthly check-ins, aimed at strengthening participants’ capacity to plan and implement research projects, produce academic publications, effectively communicate research findings, and build national and international networks. The project will significantly advance gender studies as an interdisciplinary, publicly engaged research agenda in Malaysia and beyond, building on ongoing efforts by Malaysian gender studies scholars.

This project targets the following SDGs:Reduced Inequality; Gender Equality; Decent Work and Economic Growth.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Building Excellence in Academic Collaboration, Output, and Networking in Jordan
descriptions: This project is a capacity-building initiative empowering early career researchers (ECRs) in Jordan by equipping them with skills, mentorship, and networks to produce high-quality academic outputs in the humanities and social sciences. The program focuses on women entrepreneurship and digital innovation, addressing structural barriers and fostering interdisciplinary collaboration. This project targets the following SDGs: Reduced Inequality; Decent Work and Economic Growth; Gender Equality.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Crafting impactful narratives and outputs on climate and housing in Brazil
descriptions: Extreme climate events like flooding are becoming more common due to the climate crisis, with negative impacts on urban populations. This workshop aims to amplify the voices of architecture and built environment early career researchers in Brazil to discuss strategies to help prepare for and deal with the impacts of extreme climate events and housing. This project targets the following SDGs: Reduced Inequality; Sustainable Cities and Communities; Decent Work and Economic Growth.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Building Capacity for Early Career Researchers in Ethiopia: Enhancing Academic Writing, Publishing, and Education for Peace
descriptions:
This two-year programme builds on an existing network of peace and conflict studies scholars to deliver comprehensive and conflict-sensitive academic writing workshops supporting early career researchers in Jimma, Ethiopia. The workshops seek to facilitate academic career development by enhancing research skills, academic writing, publishing, and grant writing abilities and promoting a constructive mentoring environment for early career researchers through various hands-on and practical activities. 

The project focuses on the theme of education for peace in acknowledgement of the need for Ethiopia to move away from persistent and interspersed conflict. It is hoped that the participating early career researchers will  use their critical research to transform conflict in constructive ways, influencing wider society, both at a higher, political level as well as a community, grassroots level. 

 This project targets the following SDGs: Reduced Inequality; Peace, justice and strong institutions; Gender Equality.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Strengthening individual and institutional capacity to disseminate mental health research in Nepal and Bangladesh: developing the art and techniques o
descriptions:
In response to mental health challenges and difficulties accessing mental health treatment in Nepal and Bangladesh, this project focuses on creating a sustainable pathway for capacity development to write for scientific journals and grant applications which will lead to evidence-based mental health research and delivery.

In the long term, the project will address the current gaps in the literature regarding a lack of scientifically rigours research on the prevalence of mental health problems in Nepal and Bangladesh, specific social cultural drivers of poor mental health and effective treatments to address these drivers. Such findings should inform mental health services and policy in Nepal and Bangladesh which in the long term could lead to improved quality of life of people with mental health problems and reduction in global healthcare burden. This project targets the following SDGs: Reduced Inequality; Decent Work and Economic Growth; Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Writing Workshop for African Scholars of Digital Rights
descriptions: The project is seeking to empower African early career researchers (ECRs) in Kenya, Congo, and Mali in the fields of digital rights, digital citizenship, and digital authoritarianism. This workshop series will provide ECRs with targeted training, mentoring, and editorial guidance to develop and submit high-quality journal articles. Participants will benefit from close accompaniment and advice from experienced journal editors as they refine their work, which will offer a unique contribution to literature on digital authoritarianism from an African perspective. This project targets the following SDGs: Reduced Inequality; Decent Work and Economic Growth; Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Decolonising Academic Publishing With Afro-Brazilian and Indigenous Researchers
descriptions: Through a series of in-person workshops and online specialist publication talk, the project will develop the publishing skills of Indigenous and Afro-Brazilian early career researchers, with a focus on promoting interdisciplinary and decolonial knowledge and encouraging greater take-up of such knowledge by leading international journals in the Humanities and Social Sciences. The project will  improve the career prospects for PPI (preto, pardo e indígena) scholars in Brazil, thus responding to an urgent need to increase the numbers of Black, mixed-race and Indigenous teaching and research staff at Brazilian universities. This project targets the following SDGs: Reduced Inequality; Decent Work and Economic Growth; Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: British Academy International Writing Workshops 2025 Programme Costs
descriptions:
These awards are aimed at early career researchers in Brazil, Egypt, Indonesia, Jordan, Kenya, Malaysia, Philippines, South Africa, Turkey, Thailand, Vietnam and/or Least Developed Countries, working to stimulate professional networks, develop research partnerships, encourage skills development, provide advice on career development and promote the uptake of research emanating from developing countries.

British Academy led programme activity e.g. events and workshops supporting/as part of the International Writing Workshops Programme.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Researching and Writing Gender, Spirituality and Agency in Africa
descriptions:
This award expands upon existing collaborations between the African Association for the Study of Religions (AASR) and members of the Leeds University Centre for African Studies. The writing and mentoring programme will centre around two in-person gatherings: a workshop to be held at the University of Nairobi in August 2025, and the AASR conference taking place at the University of Botswana in August 2026. 

The expected outcomes of the workshop are twofold. In the first instance, the project will contribute to training and mentoring the current generation of African scholars, specifically ensuring the participation of female scholars, who often face particular disadvantages and challenges. Secondly, it will provide participants with subject-specific expertise, skills training, networking and publishing opportunities. The second outcome is to create sustainable and collaborative reading and research networks, specifically in the field of religion and gender in Africa, with a view to promoting this important field of scholarship and strengthening the contribution of African scholars to research in this area.

The outcomes of this project strongly align with the ODA goals, such as through the fostering of interdisciplinary research that addresses critical societal and global challenges; strengthening the skills and capacity for research, innovation and knowledge exchange between UK academics and scholars in African countries, and the building of long-lasting Africa-centred scholarly networks especially through AASR structures. This project targets the following SDGs: Reduced Inequality; Gender Equality.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: International Political Sociology: Transversal Writing and Publishing II
descriptions:
Organised by the Pontifical Catholic University of Rio de Janeiro and Queen Mary University of London, these workshops will be integrated into the International Political Sociology Winter School held annually by the PUC-Rio International Relations Institute. They will focus on developing writing skills and increasing publication rates in international scientific journals for junior scholars from Latin America while fostering collaborations within academic networks across Brazil, the UK, and Europe. 

Participants will benefit from mentoring sessions, seminars, working sessions, and tutorials covering academic writing, grant applications, publishing strategies, collaborative writing, and networking. 

This project targets the following SDG: Reduced Inequality.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Art Writing and Publishing in Southeast Asia: Collectivity and Land Issues
descriptions: This program focuses on the pivotal themes of collectivity and land issues in Southeast Asia. Through workshops, seminars, and mentoring sessions, twenty early career researchers (ECRs) based in Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar Philippines, Thailand and Vietnam, explore how these themes intersect with regional art practices and social dynamics. Hosted online across five regional hubs and culminating in an in person writing intensive in Manila, the program fosters a collaborative environment, enabling ECRs to produce research publications, develop funding applications, and strengthen transnational networks. Emphasising sustainable academic ecosystems, the initiative connects researchers, publishers, and institutions to address pressing regional challenges and elevate collective local narratives. This project targets the following SDGs: Reduced Inequality; Quality Education; Sustainable Cities and Communities.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Capacity building for Syrian academics at Sham University
descriptions:
This project targets the writing and professional development of academics from Sham University in the non-regime NW of Syria. This is part of the successful Syria Programme run by the Council for At-Risk Academics (Cara). These workshops will focus on a 'training of trainers' model, building on previous training to develop a sustainable model that will allow training to reach the wider faculty of Sham University, beyond those with permission to cross the border and attend the workshops in person. Workshops will be held in 2025 in Gaziantep, in Turkey, and close to the Syrian border. They will be supported by five additional online workshops. 

Through the project, the team will: 1) build the capacity of senior academics at Sham University to develop research and writing programmes in the University; 2) build on existing gender training at Sham University in an effort to improve the proportion of women in senior leadership positions; 3) provide institutional support for Sham University as it seeks to develop the policies and processes necessary to fostering a positive environment for both teaching and research.

This project targets the following SDGs: Reduced Inequality; Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Writing for Change: Slavery, Violence and Exploitation
descriptions:
The project extends and deepens an existing exchange between Brazilian and Ghanaian  early career researchers in a program of online and in person mentorship meetings, including a 3-day writing workshop in Brazil, through which senior scholars from the UK, Brazil, and Ghana will support alumni as they develop book proposals, international journal articles, research funding applications, and acquire skills necessary to write for impact. 

Participants will receive tailored career development advice, and will be encouraged to amplify project impact through blogs and short films sharing their learning with early career researcher peers in Brazil and Ghana. 

The participants' research on slavery, violence and exploitation has strong potential to impact on public, policy, and political debate, and the project will enable the team to develop and hone this potential, providing participants with opportunities to develop skills necessary to write for impact and change. 

This project targets the following SDGs: Reduced Inequality; No Poverty; Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: From Research Assistants to Authors: A Platform for Platform Scholars in African Cities
descriptions:
"The proposed project will support early career researchers, post-doctoral fellows and doctoral students based in Africa through mentoring (both in-person workshop and virtual), expertise from a journal editorial board, publisher representatives, and wrap-around on-line support.  

The workshop will help develop a cadre of scholars to confidently engage in publishing not just within platform studies but also wider social sciences. The workshop is co-developed and co-designed with two experienced researchers who are also doctoral students from Africa. This kind of design for the training and mentorship programme is a key platform for capacity development in the region, including networking with regional and international academics and institutions. Participants will be selected from the wider African region, with a particular focus on states and institutions with lower rates of publishing in international journals.  The main outcome of the workshop would be a special issue in the Platform and Society (Sage)."

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Academic Writing Workshop for Nepalese Early Career Researchers in Humanities and Social Sciences
descriptions:
We will deliver an intensive five-day academic writing workshop to 25 early career researchers (ECRs) in Nepal. The workshop will be a series of hands-on teaching and support sessions on developing academic writing capacity, bid writing, networking, and article publishing, and will be delivered by the academic team members and journal editors. Following the workshop, participants will be supported by the team via video conferencing. Participants will be provided with constructive feedback, and their draft articles proofread and copyedited to illustrate best practice in academic English.

Participants will be drawn from the seven administrative regions of Nepal plus Kathmandu. A stratified sample of applicants will ensure parity between genders and marginalised indigenous groups. In addition to improving writing standards, we will also provide participants with the opportunity to present at the 2026 NELTA Conference.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Papers with Purpose: Writing Workshops for Research Impact with early career Health Professions Education Scholars in Southern Africa
descriptions: Health Professions Education (HPE) is a powerful field impacting on education that extends to health systems and patient care. In the global South, whilst educational and health inequities remain, HPE seeks to transform these realities through quality postgraduate training and scholarship. In South Africa, HPE research is rapidly growing, however, formal educational qualifications and scholarly outputs remain low in comparison to that of the global North. This global knowledge hierarchy has significant implications for both knowledge production for epistemic justice as well as the pragmatics of educational practices and outcomes in the health sciences that is culturally inappropriate, and contextually ineffective as ‘best evidence’ from vast contexts of the global North (Sims & Cilliers, 2023; Sims, 2023b). Therefore, our programme seeks to close these gaps with writing workshops coupled with conference participation to strengthen the networks of HPE doctoral students and early career researchers from Southern Africa.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Writing Religion and Social Transformation in Africa: publishing and mentoring workshop for early career arts, humanities and social science researche
descriptions: The Universities of Edinburgh and Malawi are collaborating with editors of Africanist journals and book-series to enhance the academic writing and publishing skills of early-career researchers (ECRs) in Southern Africa, so to diversify international academic conversations, whilst also developing ECRs’ research profiles, funding and networking capabilities. A four-day in-person writing and mentoring workshop in Malawi will be the centre of a two year programme of training and mentoring for ECRs. Focussed upon a multidisciplinary theme of critical importance, ‘Religion and Social Transformation in Africa’, researchers from arts, humanities and social science (AHSS) will prepare papers for feedback, then academic publication and public communication. ECRs will receive training in peer-review, grant application and interdisciplinary working. To build long-term AHSS research and writing capacity and career development, ECRs will be supported to undertake peer mentorship in their own institutions, be introduced to new regionally based journals and form cohorts for future collaborations.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Empowering African researchers to design competitive funding proposals: Training, mentorship and network building for African researchers working on r
descriptions: This proposal outlines a comprehensive programme aimed at empowering African researchers in Sub-Saharan Africa to secure funding for randomised evaluations of poverty alleviation interventions. The programme leverages a combination of an in-person workshop in Tanzania and ongoing virtual mentorship to enhance participants' skills in designing, securing funding for and publishing randomised evaluations. A key focus is to address the underrepresentation of African, particularly female, researchers in global economic research and publications. The programme aligns with ODA objectives, aiming to enrich the field of development economics with diverse perspectives and local context knowledge. The outcomes include increased proficiency in randomised evaluations, improved research proposal writing capabilities, and expanded professional networks. This initiative is crucial for fostering equitable and impactful research in development economics, with a long-term goal of increasing the presence of African, especially female, researchers in high-impact publications and policy-making discussions on the continent.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Training and Mentorship Programme on Academic Writing Skills in Business, Economics and Management
descriptions: Our project aims to deliver a two-year comprehensive training programme on research writing skills, through a series of structured workshops that target a large group of early career researchers (ECRs) in business, economics and management in Vietnam. The programme will also offer several mentoring sessions and one-to-one meetings between international journal editors and a selected group of Vietnamese ECRs with the potential to become pioneering scholars in their respective fields. Our proposed programme will facilitate the networking between Vietnamese ECRs and journal editors, as well as connections among researchers from private and public institutions in Vietnam. The project will promote future research collaborations and ultimately enhance research performance and grant-capture activities among Vietnamese scholars. Throughout the programme, we commit to diversity, equality and inclusion and seek to contribute to the development of the academic sector in Vietnam, as well as the country's economic development and welfare improvement.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Elevating Entrepreneurship Research: Integrating Intersectionality and Systemic Perspectives
descriptions: This ambitious programme seeks to support and develop a new generation of entrepreneurship scholars in Brazil. Recognising the complexity of entrepreneurship as a phenomenon shaped by intersecting factors of identity, systems, institutions, and culture, this initiative challenges the narrow and Western-centric focus of current research paradigms. By integrating intersectionality and ecosystem thinking, the programme aims to illuminate the intricacies of entrepreneurship, including the often-overlooked exclusionary processes and potentials for equitable and sustainable business practices. Centred around a series of writing workshops, the programme provides intensive training, mentoring, and networking opportunities. The key objectives are capacity building for complex, context-sensitive research, supporting early career scholars in producing high-quality academic output, fostering equitable North-South partnerships, and inspiring transformative changes in local academic cultures. With mentorship from renowned scholars, the programme is poised to create impactful publications and robust research networks, driving progressive change in entrepreneurship research, education, and policymaking across Latin America.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Reimagining Access to Justice: An Equitable Research Partnership with Southeast Asia
descriptions: Access to justice is central to the rule of law and sustainable development. Without access to justice people are not fully heard and they cannot effectively enforce their rights. Countries in Southeast Asia face unique access to justice challenges which call for a reimagining of current approaches to access to justice. Through a combination of hands-on feedback sessions and guided discussions on scholarly writing and publishing, these Writing Workshops bring together access to justice scholars from the United Kingdom and Southeast Asia. Our objective is to create a genuine research network among equals that will increase the representation of early career scholars from Southeast Asia and amplify their voices in contemporary legal scholarship. By making the workshop materials available online, the Writing Workshops will also reach out to a broader audience that exceeds the cycle of immediate participants and thereby have a long-term impact on academic culture.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Strengthening Academic Writing Skills, Building Networks and Fostering Mentorship for Early Career Researchers in Francophone and Anglophone West and
descriptions: Scholars suggest Africa contributes less than 1% to the global research output (Fonn et al., 2018), an estimate likely lower for the continent’s lowest income and least developed countries (LDCs). Led by a core team of African scholars based in Africa and in Diaspora, this Arican-led project leverages existing capacity building work to support, promote and advance the intellectual and professional development of African early career researchers in the lowest income and LDCs in West and Central Africa. The project undertakes an innovative structure of online sessions, in-person workshops, co-authorship and mentorship to support early career Francophone and Anglophone scholars to develop manuscripts to submit to high quality journals, gain academic self-development skills and build their networks. As a result, the project will create a strong cohort of connected African researchers who will collaborate to produce high-quality scholarship to influence debates and decisions relevant to Africa’s social development.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Amplifying the Communicative Power of Public Health Researchers in Tanzania
descriptions: African public health researchers represent one of the most dynamic communities of knowledge-creation. Drawing together diverse methodologies and theoretical frameworks across disciplinary domains in the medical, social and life sciences, their research responds to the emerging problems for the societies in which they live.  However, despite their inherent potential for impactful, translational and pathbreaking research, this frontier scientific cohort lacks consistent training in the communication skills that will enable their insights to circulate more widely and contribute to policy making and scientific innovation on a global stage. Building on a long-standing collaboration between KCL and Tanzania's Ifakara Health Institute and through intensive writing workshop combining co-curricular design, editorial expertise and peer-to-peer feedback, story-telling practice-based exercises, participants will acquire the techniques necessary to develop their ideas into fundable research proposals, produce high-quality outputs for diverse audiences, and generate lasting public health benefits for Tanzanian populations and beyond.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Addressing global challenges in academic writing: fostering scholarly pathways in Zambia, Uganda, and UK
descriptions:
This project aims to strengthen the research capacity and confidence of early career researchers (ECRs) in Zambia and Uganda. The project will provide a comprehensive support system, including mentorship, training, and networking opportunities, to enhance ECRs' research writing and communication skills. This will ultimately lead to increased publication output, improved grant funding success, and overall career development.

 Key activities include an 8-month online writing course, a mentorship scheme, an inter-institutional research seminar series, and a 3-day writing workshop. Targeting ECRs from Copperbelt University, Mountains of the Moon University, and the University of Zambia, the project is expected to boost ECRs' publication and grant success rates, fostering their research prowess and career advancement.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Interdisciplinary Writing and Capacity Building in Sustainable Food Systems Research: Developing the next generation of Brazilian ECRs
descriptions: Our programme aims to train early career researchers (ECRs) from Brazil in writing and publishing skills and to explore funding opportunities in sustainable food systems research. This is motivated by the underrepresentation of Brazilian scholars in areas such as food sustainability, food safety, food waste, economics and governance of food production and consumer behaviour. The 4-day workshop will take place in Campinas, São Paulo, Brazil, co-delivered by UK-based and Brazilian scholars. All ECRs will be allocated mentors who are editorial members of international journals and have extensive publishing and peer-reviewing experience. The programme is divided into four stages i) Pre-workshop preparation; ii) Physical workshop; iii) Post-workshop evaluation; iv) Virtual seminar. The workshop outcomes include improved writing skills and manuscript submissions by ECRs to reputable journals. Improved writing and publishing skills will lead to increased impact profile of ECRs in sustainable food systems research and opportunities to lead research projects.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: International Career Writing Programme for Researchers (ICWP)
descriptions:
We propose a highly interactive international workshop with three key components: writing for publication, career coaching, and research collaboration. The intersection of these components cultivates a supportive environment between researchers in the UK and in the Global South and promotes the uptake of their research in academic journals.

The aim of this workshop is to provide support and develop the skills of early career researchers (ECRs) from the Global South, particularly in Kenya and Senegal. To support and promote the uptake of their research in high-impact international journals, publications, and grant awards, this workshop provides the necessary knowledge to stimulate their professional networks, develop research partnerships, and advise on international career development. It does so through a train the trainer´s approach, in a blended delivery mode (online and in person) to understand the challenges and activate the opportunities for ECRs in the Global South."

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Enhance research skills and publication capacity of early career researchers from local universities in developing countries
descriptions: This workshop aims to enhance research skills and build up publication capacity in areas of social science, including (but not limited to) accounting, corporate governance, corporate social responsibility and sustainability in Southeast Asia. The workshop facilitates early career researchers (ECRs) to develop knowledge and skills for more research output and publications in high-impact international journals. Primarily, ECRs from local universities in provinces rather than in the big cities from Southeast Asia will be supported with training regarding research methodology, critical writing skills, and publishing. ECRs will be supported and mentored by a team of UK-based senior scholars who have published numerous publications in high-ranked international journals and act as editors of several international journals. The workshop also provides an opportunity for ECRs from different Southeast Asian countries to expand networking with their peers and work together as co-authors of research papers and co-applicants of research grants in the future.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Towards decolonising the publishing ecosystem through a three-tier intervention to benefit early career scholars from South Africa, Ethiopia, and Ugan
descriptions: Despite significant improvements in education levels in Africa, the continent is excluded from the inner edge of the global knowledge production structure, contributing only 1% to the world’s research output. Using action research, the proposed project aims to devise a new model of collaboration with African early career scholars through a three-tier intervention. This includes individual-level mentoring for 20 early career scholars from South Africa, Ethiopia, Uganda to enhance their publication opportunities (publishing at least 10 articles) as well as career prospects. At the journal level, we collaborate with chief editors of major international journals to secure space for our participants’ articles. Finally, at the author-editor level, we facilitate direct dialogue between African authors and chief editors to address systemic barriers to African scholarship in the publishing ecosystem. The project's impacts neatly dovetail with the selected countries’ Sustainable Development Goals (e.g. SDG 9) as well as the African Union’s vision.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Promoting African perspectives on Innovation, Digitalisation and Entrepreneurship in Africa: an interdisciplinary writing and mentoring programme for
descriptions: Building on well-established collaborations among members of the Interdisciplinary Network for Technology and Entrepreneurship Research in Africa (INTERA), this project solidifies and expands our joint commitment to supporting African Early Career Researchers (ECRs) studying Innovation, Digitalisation and Entrepreneurship in Africa. Although digital technologies and entrepreneurship have been marked as key to Africa’s development, many African scholars have a low acceptance rate when publishing on these issues in high-impact (Scimago Q2 and Q1) journals. This project brings 20  ECRs from Southern Africa studying these topics from various disciplines, like Information Systems, Anthropology and Management, together with experienced scholars from South Africa, the UK and the Netherlands to aid them in developing high-quality publications, grant proposals and international networks. After the project, we will invite the participating ECRs to join INTERA to receive long-term mentorship, peer support and encouragement to be part of editorial boards of Information Systems, Anthropology, and Management journals.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Writing For Research and Researcher Capacity-Building in Regional University Contexts (Mountains of the Moon University, Uganda and the University of
descriptions: Mountains of the Moon University (MMU) was formally recognised as the 10th Public University in Uganda in 2022. Only 6% of MMU Faculty have published papers. Despite a 10-year partnership with the University of Salford, the ability to extend teaching collaboration to research partnership has been hampered by a lack of PhD qualified/research-active Faculty. Under Government rules all new staff must have or register for PhDs.  To stimulate this MMU has appointed a core of PhD-qualified Faculty. The proposed workshops will support these Research Leaders to mentor the next generation of Early Career Researchers, building sustainable research capacity and international recognition. Activities will focus on the development of a range of writing skills with an emphasis on Writing for: (1) Conference Presentations and Publication; (2) Grant Applications; (3) Impact (Translational Research) and (4) Research-informed Teaching. Partners will collaborate to develop a PhD-by-Published-Works program to expedite the development of critical mass.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Strengthening Academic Writing and Publishing Skills for ECRs in Madagascar: Researching the Environment, Peace and Conflict
descriptions: This two-year programme builds on existing research networks around peacebuilding, conflict transformation, gender, environment, climate change, and sustainability. It draws on expertise from Madagascar, Europe and the UK.  The activities aim to create a new network of scholars supporting early career researchers in Madagascar to strengthen their research skills, academic writing, publishing and grant writing expertise. Our focus is on social sciences. Peace and conflict studies is an emerging discipline in Madagascar. A number of scholars in anthropology, social sciences focus on this now particularly in relation to environment and conflict, and how this intersects with challenges of natural resource governance and gender equality. Priority research topics will also include conflict transformation, political transformation, climate justice and adaptation, as well as structural inequalities and interdisciplinary research. We will seek to target our call for applicants to ECRs interested in developing their research in this area.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Writing for International Research Excellence for Early Career academics in South Africa (WIRE-SA)
descriptions: The Writing for International Research Excellence for Early Career academics in South Africa (WIRE-SA) project has been designed to address two interlinked priorities in South Africa. These are the persistent, historic and contemporary inequalities in health and (higher) education. The South African government’s National Development Plan has a stated goal of promoting a healthy life span, aligned to the World Health Organisation’s Sustainable Development Goals for improving health and well-being, reducing inequalities and reducing poverty. There is a distinct and vital role for social scientists to research and contribute to addressing health inequalities. The second priority focuses on inequalities in higher education through supporting the development of researchers within universities classified as ‘Historically Disadvantaged Institutions’ (HDI) in South Africa. The project team of specialists in applied social sciences, higher education and research development in a South African and international context, offers a distinct and important contribution to addressing these priorities.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Helping Early Career Researchers in Vietnam and Thailand to develop their capability to publish in high-impact journals in Development Economics
descriptions: By organising three rounds of workshops in Vietnam and Thailand and one international conference, this proposal aims to train Early Career Researchers (ECRs) in these countries to have the capacity to plan a research project, apply for a research grant, write a paper, present it at the international conference and publish papers in high-impact international journals in development economics. The project draws upon the lead/co-applicants' long experience as editors of Review of Development Economics (RDE), one of the top field journals. As ECRs in low- and middle-income countries find it hard to publish their papers in RDE due to the high desk rejection rate, the editorial board is keen to publish more papers they authored. The workshops would not only train the capacity of ECRs in Vietnam and Thailand but also create a network whereby they will develop a community to further develop and transfer publishing skills to other ECRs.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Dismantling epistemic and systemic challenges to writing and publishing: A mentorship programme for early career scholars in Southern Africa
descriptions: Research shows that the work of African-based scholars in the Humanities is underrepresented in high-impact international academic journals. Explanations for this include a lack of research funding, difficulties in gaining access and exposure to academic journals, as well as challenges in accessing the institutional knowledge of the publishing process needed to submit to high-impact international journals. It is against this background that we seek to build upon existing networks to establish a new mentoring scheme between early-career researchers in the Humanities based predominantly in Southern Africa, with senior academics and journal editors from across Africa and the globe. To this end, we hope to organize a publishing, mentoring, and grant writing programme. The programme is interdisciplinary and aims to enhance the capacity of early-career researchers in Southern Africa through interactive and collaborative activities, which will prepare participants to write articles for high-impact journals from the region.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Decolonial Writing Workshops: Empowering Brazilian and Indonesian Women Scholars to Publish Global Academic Knowledge
descriptions: Decolonial perspectives are increasingly drawing attention to the under-representation of scholars from the Global South in international academic knowledge production. This marginalisation can be further compounded for women from the Global South who may find that their gender intersects with their nationality to diminish the opportunities that they have to write and publish in global academic platforms. This project will deliver writing workshops to provide training and mentorship for 24 early-career women scholars from Brazil and Indonesia to equip them with the skills to write high quality grant bids and scholarly articles. This project aims to empower these humanities and social sciences scholars and to enhance their local research cultures. This will likely have further tangible consequences for the knowledge economies of these nations. This project will also facilitate South-South networking and collaboration between Brazilian and Indonesian scholars so as to produce new and valuable opportunities across the Global South.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Building capacity to publish in high-impact journals through mentorship and interdisciplinary training for Kenya-based early career researchers in App
descriptions:
This project will provide the infrastructure to establish interdisciplinary scholarly partnerships between Early-Career Researchers (ECRs) in Kenya and UK-based academics, across the fields of Applied Linguistics and Psychology. Among other broader aims, the primary goal is to offer Kenya-based ECRs an opportunity to receive mentoring and guidance from experienced academics and journal editors, enabling them to refine a manuscript chosen for its potential into a ready-to-submit document for a high-impact journal.
This project will consist of the following 5 stages: (S1) groundwork and selection of participants, (S2) a pre-workshop virtual mentorship program, (S3) an intensive 3-day residential workshop in Nairobi where experts will deliver training on various aspects of the publishing process, (S4) continued mentorship after the workshop to ensure that the manuscripts are further refined and prepared for submission; and within stage 4, there will be an in-person event (S5) dedicated to finalising the work and ensuring successful submission.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Enhancing Sustainability Management Research in Egypt: Challenges of Academic Writing in Emerging Economies
descriptions: This comprehensive workshop series aims to equip early career researchers from Egypt and developing countries with the necessary skills and knowledge to conduct high-quality research on sustainability management. Through a combination of a series of in-country and online workshops, Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs), and personalized online mentoring sessions, participants will gain expertise in both qualitative and quantitative research methodologies, develop strong academic writing skills, and learn how to navigate the challenges of publishing in international journals. The workshops will also foster a vibrant network of sustainability management researchers, facilitating collaboration and knowledge exchange. By empowering the next generation of sustainability researchers, this workshop series will contribute to addressing the pressing challenges of sustainable development in Egypt and beyond.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Visibilising marginalised Early Career Researchers in Peace, Conflict and Security Studies : A Writing  and Publishing Workshop for scholars from the
descriptions: This proposal seeks to build on the 2019 Workshop ‘Interdisciplinary and Collaborative Research on Peace and Security: Publishing and Grant Writing Workshop for Early Career Researchers in Eastern Africa’. The evidence base into whose knowledge matters in the field is still growing. Awareness of the need for more diversity and pluralism is more nuanced, especially in its call for decolonizing knowledge production. For the catalytic effect intended for the 2019 proposal to continue, similar initiatives are needed to support ECRs and visibilize marginalised voices from the Global South. This follow-up proposal seeks to engage with a different set of participants, including ECRs in Brazil, to provide skills that enhance the writing skills of ECRs and deepen their knowledge the publication process and research funding landscapes. The outcome of the workshop will be a South-South ECRs peer network and an opportunity to publish in two publications: a special issue journal and a Palgrave Handbook.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Minding the gap: a skill-training and close mentorship workshop to promote the professional development of early career scholars in Brazil
descriptions: International publications and networks are essential for career development; severe cuts in science, structural inequalities, and language barriers, however, have had profound implications on Brazilian researchers’ ability to publish with international academic presses and access global networks. We propose a workshop to promote the professional development of emerging political science scholars from Brazil. The programme seeks to mitigate gender, racial, and regional inequalities and will be carried out in collaboration with the Universidade Federal de Minas Gerais (UFMG). Through skills training and close mentorship, we expect that at the end of the programme, participants will: 1) have a better understanding of the publication process and feel more prepared to write papers for submission in international journals independently; 2) know about relevant international funding schemes and know-how on how to apply for them successfully; 3) have access to international networks of established scholars.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Developing Research Capacity of Early Career Researchers in West Africa: A writing and mentoring workshop for Publication
descriptions: In this project, we propose two in-person interactive workshops and two follow-up online sessions to provide a cutting-edge research training and development opportunity for Early career researchers (ECRs) in West Africa. The in-person workshops which will take place at the university of Lome and Central University in Togo and Sierra Leone in 2024 involve thirty participants selected from Togo, Sierra Leone and neighbouring French and English-speaking countries in West Africa have the following goals: (i) equip participants with the skills necessary to publish in peer-reviewed journals and write grant proposals; (ii) provide personalised mentorship, and feedback on their submitted manuscripts from experienced academics and journal editors, (iii) provide participants with opportunities to network and collaborate with their colleagues, leading scholars and journal editors to produce impactful outputs over the period of two years. (iv) provide follow-up and sustained support to participants for their submissions to international journals after the workshop.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Promoting Publication and Academic Writing towards Gender Equality research in Academia for Sustainable Development in Thailand
descriptions: This workshop series, titled, "Promoting Publication and Academic Writing towards Gender Equality in Academia for Sustainable Development in Thailand," led by the University of Derby, UK, and Srinakharinwirot University, addresses persistent gender disparities in Thai academia. Beyond a conventional workshop, it aims to catalyse a transformative cultural shift, recognizing the integral connection between gender equality, academic writing, and sustainable development. During two years, the initiative guides participants through identifying gender equality challenges in Thai academia, emphasizing stakeholder engagement from voluntary, private, and public sectors. The overarching vision is to foster an academic ecosystem where gender inclusivity is foundational, not an afterthought. Workshops focus on strategies for impactful academic writing with a gender lens, exploring collaborative avenues transcending borders. Tailored capacity-building sessions empower students and early career researchers, delving into specific approaches in academic writing and providing career development advice, including mentorship and strategies to navigate gender biases in academic publishing.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Upskilling African Early Career Researchers in Archaeology and Heritage
descriptions: Early career researchers (ECRs) in Archaeology and heritage in Africa least developed countries are challenged by inadequate mentorship, collaboration, and skills about research ethics and compliance, hindering their involvement and continuous participation in academic and research endeavours. This project will be implemented by a team of researchers from different research areas with years of experience, publication records and involvement in grant applications and funded projects. The workshops will improve the skills of six English- and six French-speaking ECRs working in five African countries, fostering wider understandings of the processes involved in conducting impactful research. Mentorship and networking opportunities to be provided will improve their career development and promote uptake and publishing of high impact journals and grant calls. Participants will present their research at Kenya Africa24 Conference in November 2024. Feedback will be collected from the participants to understand ways to improve the workshop for future implementation.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: UK-South Africa Bilateral Research Chair
descriptions: This Chair in Digital Humanities will play a key role in building capacity; creating networks; and creating intellectual agendas, a multivalent humanistic platform, grounded outreach, and new modes of material engagement and interpretative frameworks.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: British Academy ODA Global Innovation Fellowships programme 2024
descriptions: The objective of the fellowships is to embed early- and mid-career researchers to develop their skills, networks and careers in the creative and cultural, public, private and policy sectors in ISPF’s priority countries and LDCs to address challenges that require innovative approaches and solutions. This will help create new and deeper links beyond academia, so enabling knowledge mobilisation and translation, as well as individual skills development. The aim is to have a beneficial partnership between the award holder and the selected organisation in South Africa, Brazil, Egypt, Jakarta, Ethiopia, Dominican Republic of Congo, Türkiye, Nepal, Kenya, Lesotho, Indonesia, Yemen, Zambia, Jordan, and Uganda, with each able to take advantage of fresh perspectives and expand their networks and reach. Fellowships are for one-year. As well as Fellowships related to thematic areas of health and wellbeing, transformative technology and global order, the Academy would expect to support a proportion of the awards on climate-related fellowships.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Gender, armed conflict and peacemaking
descriptions:
The award holder’s research will significantly impact Conciliation Resources' policymaking by providing deeper insights into the roles of female ex-combatants in post-conflict transitions (and supports Sustainable Development Goal 5). This will inform the design of inclusive reintegration strategies and frameworks for political engagement, particularly in Ethiopia’s Somali region. Using ethnographic methods, the project will explore women's personal and political transitions, directly supporting Conciliation Resources’ work with the Ogaden National Liberation Front (ONLF) and its peacebuilding efforts. The research will also offer valuable insights into the root causes of Somali nationalist resistance, helping to shape policies that address the specific needs of marginalized communities in Ethiopia.

Furthermore, the project will analyse the Ethiopian government’s role as a ‘security state’ and its impact on women’s experiences within insurgent and post-war contexts, contributing to gender-sensitive peacebuilding strategies. The findings will help strengthen advocacy for inclusive peacebuilding and transitional justice frameworks.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Transformative Technologies
descriptions:
This fellowship proposal, in collaboration with Ashoka Brazil, aims to address digital disengagement among older adults in Brazil, an upper-middle-income country, and other low-and-middle-income countries (LMICs) facing similar challenges. With an ageing population and increasing digitalisation, these regions experience inequality, illiteracy, and prolonged health issues, particularly among older adults. The fellowship aligns with Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) 3, 11, 4, 8, and 10, focusing on promoting healthy lives, reducing inequality, and fostering inclusive economic growth.

The fellowship will explore the digital disengagement of older adults, particularly those facing multiple disadvantages. The research aims to develop a framework to enhance inclusive digital services that cater to the needs of older adults. This will address gaps in digital equity, ensuring access to essential services and improving health outcomes, digital economy participation, and social inclusion.

The findings will be disseminated through academic publications, training materials, and policy briefs, influencing both local and national policy on digital equity. The project will also promote welfare by recommending policy changes that improve older adults' access to services and digital tools. The framework's impact will extend to other LMICs, offering scalable solutions to improve digital engagement and reduce inequality.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Tackling mental health challenges faced by young creatives in East Africa
descriptions: This Fellowship will enhance understanding of the mental health challenges facing young creatives in East Africa, investigating the critical role Santuri East Africa plays in sustaining the cultural ecosystem and developing innovative approaches/solutions to strengthen the resilience of the East African creative sector. It will strengthen Santuri’s capacity to support the mental health and wellbeing of young creatives in East Africa. By integrating wellbeing resources into their programs, Santuri will improve staff and community resilience, fostering personal and professional growth for emerging artists. The fellowship will also contribute to regional knowledge exchange, positioning Santuri as a leader in arts and mental health. Long-term impacts include sustainable wellbeing interventions, new partnerships, and the creation of a replicable wellbeing model for other arts organizations. The project will enhance Santuri’s operational resilience and contribute to the broader development of East Africa’s creative industries. This fellowship supports the Sustainable Development Goals related to reducing inequality, and good health and wellbeing.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Global Order, Geopolitics and International Affairs
descriptions:
The main beneficiaries of this project, undertaken in partnership with AmazoniAlerta, will be Indigenous communities in Brazil. The purpose of this fellowship is addressing the legislative challenges impacting their rights. It also extends its impact internationally by tracking opportunities for Indigenous advocacy at regional and global levels. The project monitors legislative proposals in Brazil and calls for input from international human rights bodies, ensuring Indigenous voices are represented in decision-making processes.

Aligned with key Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), the project supports SDG 16 (Peace, Justice, and Strong Institutions) by promoting transparency and strengthening Indigenous participation in legal frameworks, SDG 15 (Life on Land) by protecting Indigenous land rights, SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities) by fostering economic and environmental benefits, and SDG 17 (Partnerships for the Goals) by building coalitions among Indigenous and civil society organizations.

The project’s key pathways to impact include improving legal protections for Indigenous peoples, strengthening advocacy, and enhancing international engagement. By monitoring and disseminating insights on legislative proposals, the project allows Non-Governmental Organisations to intervene and advocate for Indigenous rights, preventing harmful changes. It also bridges domestic, regional, and international legal systems, contributing to stronger legal protections and sustainable development. Additionally, the fellowship builds sustainable advocacy capacity by creating accessible public databases for strategic, evidence-based advocacy, benefiting Indigenous communities both in Brazil and globally.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Environment, Sustainability & Nature
descriptions: The proposed project, rooted in the Kaapora Indigenous and Environmental Film Festival, bridges Indigenous cinema, eco-activism, and environmental humanities. Focusing on Brazil's Atlantic Forest, it prioritises local, collaborative knowledge production, amplifying Indigenous narratives on climate change and ecological preservation. Through participatory filmmaking workshops, the project empowers communities to reflect on their environmental concerns while generating valuable insights into arts-based eco-activism. Collaborating with Indigenous organisations and activists, the initiative fosters sustainable dialogue, producing films and resources to engage wider audiences on environmental issues. The project’s innovative approach supports long-term knowledge exchange and cultural empowerment, shaping future collaborations in environmental scholarship. This project supports SDGs 10 and 13.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Environment, Sustainability & Nature
descriptions: This fellowship will provide vital knowledge on biodiversity credit markets’ (BCMs') risks and opportunities for Indigenous and pastoralist communities in Kenya.
